articles.title: Jonah Lea'ea Pick Six Sparks Big House Rout in Michigan Win
articles.summary: The Utah transfer’s instinctive third-quarter interception ignited a scoring barrage, turning a sloppy start into a dominant blowout as the Wolverines flexed...
articles.body:
The Big House momentum can turn in an instant, and senior defensive tackle Jonah Lea'ea proved that on Saturday afternoon. Michigan took care of business with a 52-17 victory over UTEP, but the path to that convincing final score required a spark after a sloppy, penalty filled start. That spark arrived late in the third quarter courtesy of a huge defensive highlight from the Utah transfer.

With Michigan holding a 38-14 lead late in the third frame, UTEP quarterback EJ Colson dropped back, attempting to set up a screen pass to get the Miners moving. Lea'ea read the play perfectly from his interior spot on the defensive line. The 6-5, 290 pound lineman sniffed out the design, got his hands into the passing lane, and picked off the pass.

Lea'ea did not just settle for the takeaway. Securing the ball, he rumbled into the end zone for a pick six touchdown, capping off a lightning fast scoring stretch for the Wolverines. In a matter of 78 seconds, Michigan went from holding a comfortable lead to completely blowing the game open at 45-14, standardizing control before heading into the final quarter.

The explosive play capped off a complete defensive effort from Lea'ea, who continues to establish his presence in the middle of Michigan's front. After transferring in from Utah during the offseason, Lea'ea was brought to Ann Arbor to provide proven experience, anchor the run defense, and push the pocket. His instincts on the screen pass showcased the veteran poise Michigan coaches hoped to see when he joined the program.

While Michigan struggled with early turnovers and sloppy execution during parts of the first half, the defense stepped up when needed to stifle any potential UTEP threat. The third quarter turned into an absolute barrage for the Maize and Blue, highlighted by Bryce Underwood connecting with Andrew Marsh for a touchdown just moments before Lea'ea delivered his defensive score.

For Lea'ea, the pick six marks a signature moment early in his Wolverine career. Beyond the stat sheet, defensive linemen rarely get the chance to celebrate in the end zone with the ball in their hands, making the sequence one of the loudest crowd reactions of the afternoon inside Michigan Stadium.

As Michigan improves to 3-0 on the young season, defensive depth and opportunistic plays will remain crucial with Big Ten play looming next week against Iowa. If Jonah Lea'ea can keep making game changing plays up front, Michigan's defense will be well positioned for the tough conference battles ahead.

articles.title: Watch Lane Kiffin mercilessly booed upon arrival for LSU-Ole Miss game
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin’s highly anticipated return to Ole Miss got off to a hostile start as boos rained down on the LSU coach before Saturday night’s top-10 showdown w...
articles.body:
The college football season is in its third week, and one of the most anticipated battles of the season is about to commence. LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin makes his long-awaited return to Oxford to take on his former Ole Miss Rebels team.

It's bound to be an emotional night in Oxford, and there's no doubt what kind of reception Kiffin would receive. Now, that highly anticipated welcome has been captured on camera.

Kiffin was captured on camera entering Vaught-Hemingway Stadium , and the boos rained down. It was a heavy pour as the Ole Miss crowd welcomed Kiffin back to the stadium of the team he left for LSU late last season.

Lane Kiffin arrives at Ole Miss to loud boos 🗣️ (Via @glenwest21 ) pic.twitter.com/pTQFPPebn7 — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) September 19, 2026

Lane Kiffin arrives at Ole Miss to loud boos 🗣️ (Via @glenwest21 ) pic.twitter.com/pTQFPPebn7

Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) September 19, 2026

While Kiffin's return has dominated the headlines, the matchup itself carries significant implications for both programs. No. 7 LSU and No. 8 Ole Miss enter Saturday night's showdown unbeaten at 2-0. This is the first time since 1962 that the two programs have met while both ranked inside the top 10.

📍Oxford pic.twitter.com/7xEHwetQTF — LSU Football (@LSUfootball) September 19, 2026

LSU Football (@LSUfootball) September 19, 2026

LSU enters its first SEC game of the season after dominating Clemson and Louisiana Tech . Ole Miss has also looked strong through two games, defeating Louisville and UNC-Charlotte. Now, both teams face their first major test of the season with the national spotlight squarely on Oxford.

The stakes extend well beyond Kiffin's return. A victory would give either team an early advantage in the SEC race. I could also provide a valuable resume boost as the season progresses. With multiple SEC teams currently ranked inside the top 10, every conference victory could become increasingly important when the league title picture and College Football Playoff race take shape.

LSU football coach Lane Kiffin takes the field before his team's game against Louisiana Tech at Tiger Stadium on Sept. 12, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

That makes Saturday's game about far more than revenge or an uncomfortable reunion. LSU wants to prove it can immediately contend under Kiffin. However, Ole Miss has an opportunity to protect its home field and make a statement against its former coach.

Kiffin's return may be the story everyone is talking about, but the result could become one of the defining moments of the early SEC season.

articles.title: Manchester Sees the Birth of a New Star of World Boxing. Pat Brown is the Man to Watch
articles.summary: A year on from the death of Ricky Hatton, his hometown has another winner to get behind
articles.body:
It really could have been scripted. A year after the death of their hero, Ricky Hatton, Manchester's boxing fans have received a gift in the form of the big-punching cruiserweight, Pat "The Bomber" Brown. He's just as down-to-earth as Ricky, and he throws a body shot that the old "Hitman" would have been proud of.

Local boy, Pat Brown is just as devoted to his fans as they are to him, but he refuses to use the word "fans". He prefers to call them "my people".

His arrival as the new hope came in a thrilling encounter with another proud and undefeated cruiser, the 6'6 southpaw, John Hedges from Essex. It's rare that we get to see two top prospects risking their undefeated records, so enormous credit must go to the pair of them, and to their promoter, Matchroom's Eddie Hearn.

Hedges perhaps deserves even more credit for agreeing to take on Brown in his backyard at Manchester's Co-OP Live Arena.

Brown only had six fights to his name going into this contest, but he was a solid favourite, by virtue of his crushing power in both hands and his amateur pedigree, which included an appearance at the 2024 Olympic Games.

Brown showed that the power that demolished lesser opposition was no less of a problem for a top operator like Hedges. The Essex man may have shaded the first couple of rounds with his decent jab, but there was no doubt as to who was doing the real damage. Almost every punch Brown landed had a visible effect.

Brown's trainer, Jamie Moore knew that the bulldozing style that he'd employed up to now would not be adequate against the rangy and clever Hedges. After a somewhat over-eager start, John adopted a more patient approach and started to find the target with his own jab. Despite a substantial disadvantage in height and reach, he even managed to outjab the jabber - and a southpaw jabber at that.

Brown was also mixing in shots to Hedge's elongated body. Every one of them looked painful.

In the end, it was hooks to the body that closed the show, leaving the brave young Hedges writhing in agony on the canvas in the sixth round.

The former cruiserweight champion Tony Bellew said that Brown had the potential not just to win a world title, but to unify the division. It seems crazy to talk that way about a seven-fight prospect, but it's easy to get carried away after a performance like that.

Eddie Hearn said Brown would probably end up as a heavyweight. But Jamie Moore sought to bring everyone back down to earth by saying that Brown should be brought along very slowly. Everyone in British boxing is mindful of what happened to Moses Itauma a couple of weeks ago, after being thrown in with a top heavyweight in only his 14th fight.

Brown needs rounds to fully develop, but it will be hard finding opponents under world title level who are durable enough to provide them.

It'll be a long journey for Pat Brown, but one made easier by the assured support of some of the most passionate boxing fans in the world.

articles.title: Game Thread: TCU Football vs. Arkansas State
articles.summary: Horned Frogs battle Red Wolves in non-conference finale
articles.body:
The TCU Horned Frogs (1-1; 0-0 Big 12) wrap up its non-conference slate, hosting the Arkansas State Red Wolves (1-1; 0-0 Sun Belt) at home in Fort Worth's Amon G. Carter Stadium. This is the first game formally replacing the Battle for the Iron Skillet as the SMU-TCU rivalry gets indefinitely paused. Each squad has it's sole win over an FCS opponent and a loss to the only FBS opponent it has faced, each looking to move above .500 for the first time this season.

Arkansas State is coming off a win over West Georgia where its defense scored two touchdowns and the Red Wolves offense found the endzone twice by air and three times on the ground. QB Trey Owens had a tough outing in the opener vs. Memphis, throwing four interceptions in the loss to the Tigers, but bounced back nicely the next week by completing 76% of his passes. ASU has a few RBs that can get the job done on the ground, led by Kenyon Clay who has two scores on the season. Defensively, the Red Wolves are led by tackling machine Robert Stevens at linebacker. He already has 15 tackles, a sack, a forced fumble, and an interception this season and the TCU offense will need to know where he is on every play.

TCU took full advantage of its get-right opportunity against FCS Grambling State last week, bouncing back in a big way after falling flat vs. UNC in Ireland. QB Jaden Craig showed real connection with his TEs and aired it out all over the field for 391 yards and 4 TDs. The TCU defense picked up a pair of interceptions with Teon Parks returning one for 67 yards and a score.

Can the Horned Frogs close the out-of-conference portion of its schedule with a win? Join the conversation in the comment section below as we ride the game day rollercoaster together. Go Frogs!

articles.title: Lauren Steadman: How Paralympic gold led to Celebrity MasterChef glory, career, net worth and personal life in focus
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lauren Steadman has added another major title to a career already filled with Paralympic medals. The British athlete won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 aft.
articles.body: Lauren Steadman has added another major title to a career already filled with Paralympic medals. The British athlete won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 after beating Olympic weightlifter Emily Campbell and Love Island star Shakira Khan in the BBC One final. Steadman impressed judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli with a three-course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision. The victory gives the 33-year-old another television success after Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. But away from TV, Steadman’s biggest achievements have come in swimming and paratriathlon.How did Lauren Steadman win Celebrity MasterChef 2026 with Emily Campbell and Shakira KhanSteadman won the Celebrity MasterChef 2026 final on September 18 after the three finalists were asked to cook a three-course meal for Dent and Locatelli. The series started with 15 celebrities before the competition was reduced to the final three.Her menu began with pan-fried scallops in chilli butter, served with coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and fresh apple batons. For the main course, she prepared beef Wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallots, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and red wine jus.The dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream. It proved to be a key moment in the final. Locatelli praised the pudding, while Dent also spoke highly of Steadman’s food.Steadman was visibly emotional after hearing the result. She said: “This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal. There haven’t been many moments when I have been left speechless but this is one of them.”The final followed several demanding challenges during the series. Steadman had already cooked for guests at Crufts and taken part in the Chef’s Table at The Ritz.Steadman’s final menu helped her secure the trophy, while also noting her earlier Paralympic success.What are Lauren Steadman’s Paralympic achievements and sports recordsBefore becoming a television regular, Steadman built her name in elite sport. Born in Peterborough, she started swimming at a young age and represented Great Britain at the Beijing 2008 Paralympic Games when she was 15.She returned to the pool at London 2012. Her results did not bring a Paralympic medal, but the experience helped shape what came next.Steadman later moved into paratriathlon after her uncle, who is also a triathlete, encouraged her to try the sport. Her first British triathlon came in 2011, when she finished second.Her first Paralympic triathlon medal came at Rio 2016, where she won silver in the sport’s Paralympic debut. Five years later, she went one step further at Tokyo 2020, winning gold in the women’s PTS5 event.At Paris 2024, Steadman returned to the podium with bronze in the same classification. That gave her a full set of Paralympic triathlon medals: silver, gold and bronze.According to ParalympicsGB, Steadman is a three-time World Champion and has won eight European titles. She was also appointed MBE in the 2022 New Year Honours for services to triathlon.What TV shows has Lauren Steadman appeared on after her Paralympic careerSteadman’s television career began long before Celebrity MasterChef. In 2018, she joined Strictly Come Dancing with professional dancer AJ Pritchard. She reached the semi-finals and became the first female contestant with a disability to take part in the BBC show.Her next major television challenge came with Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. Steadman reached the final stage of the competition and was later crowned a joint winner of the series.She also appeared on Richard Osman’s House of Games before taking on Celebrity MasterChef in 2026.The television appearances have given audiences a different look at Steadman outside competition. Strictly tested her dancing, SAS put her through demanding physical and mental challenges, while MasterChef moved her into a completely different setting.Her professional work also includes motivational speaking and business activity. Steadman’s official website describes her work around mindset, performance and helping people deal with perceived barriers. She is also linked to Sizu, a motivational wellness clothing brand.What is Lauren Steadman’s net worth, education and personal lifeAccording to LatestCelebArticles, Lauren Steadman’s net worth is estimated at between $1 million and $5 million. However, the website does not provide financial records or details showing how the figure was calculated, so the estimate cannot be independently confirmed. Her income is linked to her sporting career, television appearances, sponsorships and other professional work.The University of Portsmouth’s profile of the Paralympic champion confirms that, alongside her sporting and television career, she has also been involved in entrepreneurial work.Her income has come from several areas over the years, including elite sport, television work, sponsorships, speaking engagements and business projects. Her exact earnings from Celebrity MasterChef and her other television appearances have not been publicly disclosed.Steadman also has a strong academic background. She studied Psychology at the University of Portsmouth, graduating with a first-class degree in 2014. She later completed an MSc in Business and Management with distinction in 2017.The University of Portsmouth has highlighted both degrees in its profiles of Steadman. The university also notes her sporting achievements, including her Rio silver, Tokyo gold and Paris bronze.Away from sport and television, Steadman has generally kept her personal life private. She has spoken publicly about the role her family played in her early sporting journey, while her uncle was the person who encouraged her to try triathlon after her swimming career.Claims about her current relationship should be treated carefully because reliable public sources do not provide enough information to independently confirm the reported details about a boyfriend named Danny.Steadman has built a career across several very different fields. She went from a teenage Paralympic swimmer to a world-class paratriathlete, won gold at Tokyo 2020, returned for bronze in Paris, appeared on major British television shows and has now added the Celebrity MasterChef trophy to her record.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Does Indiana's defense have problems after second straight shutout? Overreactions from win vs WKU
articles.summary: It's time to overreact: How many Hoosiers are Heisman contenders? Nick Marsh had his best game, and is the defense ready for Big Ten play? What we learned.
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana started sluggishly but accelerated away from Western Kentucky in a 38-0 win Saturday, finishing the No. 4 Hoosiers ' nonconference slate.

Classifying this as an overreaction probably depends on your particular concern.

It's two games in three now that the Hoosiers haven't looked quite so dominant as we expected at the line of scrimmage. Indiana's secondary still looks like a work in progress, which, considering injuries and the lived experience of some early season busts last year, is perhaps not hugely surprising.

Perhaps most notably, IU isn't forcing turnovers at nearly the rate it did a season ago. The Hoosiers gained 30 takeaways in 64 quarters last year, but have just three through 12 so far this fall.

You can find some concern in all that and still recognize that this is a unit that's allowed 16 points through three games. It shouldn't look like a finished product in September. But it can get better, and probably will.

This isn't an overreaction purely because the last guy won it, and the one before was a fringe candidate as well. Still, we won't preemptively anoint anyone as New York-bound.

Josh Hoover (649 yards, 10 touchdowns, zero interceptions) has looked very good through his first three games as a Hoosier. Even allowing for the competition, he's looked calm, poised and comfortable, and made some high-difficulty throws. His connections with Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh continue to expand, and the offense continues to build around Hoover himself.

Cignetti will have points of criticism. Not least a pair of missed throws to Marsh — one on a fourth-down slant route and the other a sideline vertical — that might have been touchdowns Saturday, if they'd been on target. Like Fernando Mendoza before him, Hoover still has room to grow in this offense. If he does, the same attention Mendoza got will find its way back to Bloomington.

Don't laugh at this one. If Jeremiah Smith is on the shortlist, Becker should be too.

He's got six touchdowns through three games. His highlight reel expands by the week. We know what he's capable of, even against better competition than this.

It's obviously very difficult for a receiver to get Heisman traction. We're not suggesting Becker will win it. But if we're going to include a player like Smith in those conversations, Becker probably deserves a place as well.

This isn't an overreaction at all. He was sharp, explosive and dangerous.

Cignetti will harp on his fumble, which Marsh was admittedly fortunate to recover. But after two weeks of Hoover-to-Becker dominating the passing game, it should be broadly encouraging to see Marsh step into a leading role this week. Becker led all Hoosiers with 127 yards receiving, but Marsh's 10 targets were tops on the team, and he finished with seven catches for 81 yards. His downfield blocking remains outstanding as well.

The more that turns into a two-man receiving attack, the more dangerous this offense becomes.

This is hardly an overreaction. This team has room to grow, but it's also clearly one of the best teams in the conference once again.

Perhaps it would be more accurate to say this team needs Big Ten play. It's learned all it can from these largely forgettable nonconference games . Indiana goes forward or not based on what it does against someone its own size from here going forward.

The Hoosiers are ready for league play, but more specifically, the season is ready for league play. This team needs those tests, and we'll learn a lot more once they arrive.

articles.title: Monmouth football avenges season-ending loss with 1st road win at Albany since '06
articles.summary: Monmouth football was relentless as they erased the memories of last year's season-ending loss by beating Albany 28-20 on the road on Saturday.
articles.body:
The flashes of brilliance were always there. In the spring showcase, and in fall camp, there were scattered moments that foreshadowed a breakthrough season for Monmouth football's defense. On Saturday against a perennially frustrating foe, they turned in a masterclass performance from the opening series to a final goal line stand.

The Hawks set the tone on the road against SUNY Albany when JJ Lewis tipped the first pass attempt of the game and Ryan Russo intercepted it for a 30-yard pick six. Four quarters later, the defense made a goal line stand that culminated with a Hunter Watson sack on 4th-and-goal from the 3-yard line. It was the relentless performance necessary to erase the memories of last year's season ending loss as Monmouth beat Albany 28-20.

Monmouth U football wins season opener against Sacred Heart U 31-24

"This was for all of our guys. Monmouth has played Albany since I can remember," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "It's a big game and our guys knew that. This is for our alumni. This is for the guys who played last year, who had their last game end poorly. And then this is for these guys, they're coming up here and winning in a tough environment."

And on top of that recent history, it was the Hawks ' (2-2) first win in Upstate New York against Albany (2-2) in two decades, dating back to a 19-0 win back in 2006. It was both a turning point for a new chapter and a defensive homage to that shutout victory 20 years ago.

The touted front four delivered on its considerable potential with lights out performances on third down. Mo Keshen, the star of that spring showcase , led the way with 1.5 sacks. In addition to the tip that led to the pick six, Lewis added his own sack. Donovan Dyson had a strip sack, but the Hawks couldn't recover the fumble. Hunter Watson added his sack and Jahide Lesaine had a half sack in addition to several pressures. Jaeden Jones turned another star performance with an interception and a team-high seven solo tackles.

"It's really 11 guys, in each of their minds, deciding they're gonna do the job at high level," Gallo said. "Because at some point, there's only so many schemes. It's just 11 guys playing as one. That's what we've been trying to push on. And having confidence that we can play the ball in the air and confidence that, I can rush this guy because the other guy's got the other guy . It's just 11 guys playing as one."

There were some of the same maddening lapses that held the Hawks back in their previous three games, particularly the two losses to Western Michigan and Tennessee Tech. Albany's first touchdown came after a fake punt, another frustrating special teams lapse. But it took a spirited effort for the Great Danes just to remain competitive against a Monmouth defense that tallied six sacks, eight tackles for loss and two interceptions. Former Monmouth player Matthew Iuvara had to make a tightrope catch on a heave to the corner of the end zone to get Albany's second touchdown.

That was also a testament to the way the Hawks seized control on the road in the opening quarter. After that pick six, that forced a three-and-out on the following possession. Frankie Weaver then unleashed one of his best passes of the season on a deep ball to Gavin Nelson to extend the Monmouth lead to 14-0.

"It was just great ball placement," Gallo said. "We had to make our shots count. We made our first two shots count, which was good. Good routes, good ball placement, speed. Those three things, when they were work well, can do explosive plays."

The fake punt happened on the last play of the first quarter and led to an eventual 10-yard touchdown run by Albany's Joey Koch. But the Hawks remained resilient, and Weaver ripped another deep ball that might've been even better than the first one on a post to Tra Neal for a 60-yard touchdown with 11:35 left in the second quarter. Neal had his second straight game with more than 100 receiving yards as he finished with 138 on five catches.

The improvement was evident across the board as Monmouth's execution was consistently better than that of Albany. They opened the second half with a 10-play, 80-yard drive that ended with a short touchdown run by Nazir Treadwell. The more intricate offensive designs and game plans are still to come, but the Hawks are honing the bread and butter plays that can be the foundation for future success.

Weaver was well on his way to producing his best performance of the season, but got a bit overzealous with two second half interceptions. The first one was particularly costly, as it came in the red zone as the Hawks were on the verge of putting the game out of reach late in the third quarter. But while those two mistakes look glaring on paper, he was 11-of-13 for 200 yards and two touchdowns aside from those lapses.

"He made some really good throws," Gallo said. "And now it's seeing these two and knowing, hey if I'm under duress, throw the ball away, take the sack if we have to . It's those little things. But he made so many strides."

And the unsung heroes of the day were the offensive line and the running backs. There was only one "explosive" run (a run of 20-plus yards) in the game, but Elijah Jennings and Kenny Smith combined for 156 rushing yards on 31 carries. Smith sealed the victory with an incredible effort on a carry on 3rd-and-7. And in addition to clearing space in the running game, the offensive line didn't allow a sack.

It was an ideal performance for Monmouth as they improve to 2-0 in CAA play and got an additional boost when Stony Brook stunned league favorite Rhode Island in a 56-24 upset, clearing the way for a wide-open race to the conference title. Incrementally, the win is big for the Hawks as they prepare to face a tough Dartmouth team on the road next week after the Big Green nearly upset No. 7 Lehigh, but lost 24-20 on a last-second interception.

But sometimes, it's just important to count the victories that mean more in their individuality than they do in the grand scheme.

"We're 2-0 in conference, we're in the spot we want to be in. Gotta keep getting better," Gallo said. "But for the program, the alumni, for the guys last year, for our team this year—it was all of those things. I'm very happy and proud of that."

articles.title: Browns fans don’t expect an improvement this week, due to worst QB situation in NFL
articles.summary: Cleveland fans are already extremely pessimistic. It’s only Week 2.
articles.body:
After their loss to open the season, Cleveland Browns fans lost confidence in the direction of the team. Specifically, they had a decrease of 34 percentage points from week-to-week, dropping from 55% confidence to 21% confidence.

I think fans were willing to deal with the usual frustrations from QB Deshaun Watson for a couple of weeks, with the assumption that QB Shedeur Sanders ' shot at starting again would come sooner rather than later. However, it's one thing to lose a close game with bad quarterback play. It's another thing to get completely blown out by the second quarter, with horrible defense all-around playing a factor in that blowout too. How can a team look so lost and uninspired in Week 1?

We asked one other question this week, which asked if fans expected the Browns to at least have a better performance in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . I phrased the question in that way because I thought, "If I ask my usual question of who will win the game, 99% of people are going to vote Tampa." I thought my phrasing would lend to more optimism, but only 29% of fans think that Cleveland will play better this week. The rest are expecting a rinse and repeat of the same degree of shitty football, as Todd Monken would put it.

There was also a national poll this week that asked which team had the worst quarterback situation. There were some good contenders on the list — the Browns, Falcons , Dolphins, Vikings, and Patriots — but the Browns ran away with it easily at 67%, followed by the Falcons at 19%.

According to FanDuel , the Browns are 8.5 point underdogs against the Buccaneers this week, with the over/under being 41.5.

articles.title: Week 2 gambling preview: Bet on George Pickens, plus other picks
articles.summary: What are your favorite NFL props for this week?
articles.body:
The second Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will be here soon. It's time to sit back, relax, and enjoy some football. Before the second Sunday festivities of the year kick off, here are our gambling picks for the Week 2 slate.

Both the Bears and the Vikings exploded on offense in Week 1. Chicago scored a league-high 59 points while the Vikings put up 39, led by backup quarterback Carson Wentz . While the Vikings' defense will be a much more significant challenge for Chicago than Carolina's defense was, their offense looks like it's going to be hard to slow down this season.

Between Ben Johnson's aggressiveness and the Bears' lack of ability on the defensive side of the ball, it seems almost certain they will be in high-scoring affairs nearly every week. Just like they did in Week 1, look for both teams to score 24+ points and hit the over.

Week 1 was an absolute disaster for Drake Maye and the New England Patriots . As bad as the loss to Seattle was, a Week 2 home contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers should be a fairly soft landing spot. After losing star wideout A.J. Brown to an ankle injury, look for Maye to do it himself against Pittsburgh on Sunday and use his legs quite often.

Maye has surpassed 25 rushing yards in eight of his last 10 games played, and he should have a good chance to do so again on Sunday.

The Los Angeles Rams and New York Giants are coming off complete opposite outcomes in Week 1. The Rams, who are the heavy Super Bowl favorite, got dominated by the San Francisco 49ers in a shocking outcome. The Giants handed a division rival a beating of their own, taking it to our Dallas Cowboys .

This week, water finds its level on both sides, and the Rams get back to looking like the team we all thought they would be. If that happens, star wideout Puka Nacua will be the catalyst on the offensive side of the ball. Look for Nacua to dominate against New York's secondary, putting together a big day in a Rams' win.

Washington Commanders at Dallas Cowboys -4.5

The Pick : George Pickens 70+ receiving yards (+116)

After a quiet Week 1, look for George Pickens to break out on Sunday against a below-average Washington secondary. Pickens may draw the matchup against Commanders' cornerback Mike Sainristil throughout the course of this game, where he has a clear advantage.

Let us know what you think about our picks in the comments section.

articles.title: Chicago Bears vs. Minnesota Vikings Game Picks and Predictions
articles.summary: The WCG staff, including @GOOCH1701, @SamHouseholder, @iamcogs, and @wiltfongjr, makes their picks for the Bears vs. Vikings game!
articles.body:
Hello Chicago Bears fans! We are back with our roundtable on Week 2 predictions of the Chicago Bears' home opener against the Minnesota Vikings . This week, the Bears face one of the NFL's most unpredictable defenses as Brian Flores matches wits with Ben Johnson. Johnson's offenses have tended to get the better of Flores coordinated defense over the years; however, Flores' defense gave the Bears fits last year in their two games, which they split. What happens when the unstoppable force meets the immovable object?

We are going to find out on Sunday at 12:00pm CST.

Lester : Bet the over again this week as the Bears will win 34 to 27. The running game will be the story, as D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai will again be over 200 combined yards, and Caleb Williams will add 50 more on scrambles. The quick passing game will find Colston Loveland for a half dozen catches, and Caleb will hit one massive deep shot to Luther Burden III . Grady Jarrett picks up his first sack of the year, and the Bears get three more takeaways.

Sam : The forecast calls for a rainy Sunday at Soldier Field. All the more reason for Ben Johnson to rely on his ground game to neutralize Minnesota's blitz. Hopefully, Caleb has been practicing his wet ball drills, and they can stay clean from turnovers. I think it could be a slog at times and a bit lower scoring. Bears 27, Vikings 23

Gary : Bears 28, Vikings 17. Heavy dose of the ground game makes QB1's life easier; Carson Wentz takes a couple sacks, loses a fumble, and throws a pick. The game gets iced with a Caleb Williams touchdown pass. Bears move to their rightful spot: 1st place in the NFC North.

Gooch : Bears 42, Vikings 10. I know most analysts are predicting a major regression in the Bears' scoring this week given the Vikings' defense, but I don't think Flores will find as much success this week with his pressure scheme against Caleb as he did against Jordan Love . Caleb will throw for 300 yards and 3 touchdowns. Colston Loveland finally gets on the board with two touchdown catches and 80 yards receiving. Swift adds a rushing touchdown and puts up another hundred-yard game. On defense, both Sweat and Booker notch a sack and several QB pressures as the Bears find Wentz a much easier target in the pocket than Bryce Young was in Carolina. Bears force Wentz to throw two interceptions, putting the Vikings behind the eight ball for most of the game.

Superfans: If I didn't know any better, I'd say Gooch was a distant relative on Busha Swerski's side with a prediction like that. Actually, I may need to check the family tree to be sure he's not a second cousin, because a first cousin wouldn't have gone with such a close score prediction. A first cousin would have brought another 50-burger to the party with some beefs and giardiniera, and called it: Bears 56, Vikings 3.

articles.title: Penn State postgame report card: Grading Nittany Lions vs. Buffalo
articles.summary: Penn State dominated Buffalo 55-13, but the real test begins next week as the Nittany Lions start Big Ten play.
articles.body:
The Nittany Lions had a comprehensive 55-13 victory over the Buffalo Bulls to close out their non-conference schedule. However, there were some things the Nittany Lions could improve on as they head into their Big Ten opener. Here is what the postgame report card looks like for the Nittany Lions ' win against Buffalo.

While there was nothing truly bad about Rocco Becht 's performance this week, it definitely didn't feel the same as the past two weeks when he was firing on all cylinders. While he still threw for two touchdowns and was 11-for-19 with 212 yards, he had some miscues and overthrows. In fact, if it weren't for some spectacular catches made by his receivers, Becht may not have had as decent a stat line. Both Alex Manske and Connor Barry did come into the game for mop-up duty, but for the first time, it didn't feel like it was because of Becht, but because of the team's collective performance as well.

This was much more like it from the Penn State running backs. The Nittany Lions RBs combined for 295 yards after there were growing concerns around the run game from the first two games of the season. James Peoples contributed 59 yards and two touchdowns, and Carson Hansen and Cam Wallace got in the scoring action as well. However, the revelation of the day was Quinton Martin Jr. , who was the leading rusher with exactly 100 yards, including a 61-yard run in the first half. Matt Campbell will be delighted that the running game has come to life before Big Ten play.

The only player elevating this group is, of course, Koby Howard . The breakout star for the Nittany Lions continues to shine in this offense, scoring both on a 70-yard run and a 16-yard end around trick play. Other than that, there was really nothing to write home about in the pass game. Chase Sowell did have a highly impressive catch, and Andrew Rappleyea caught a touchdown pass, but this was all about the run game for the Nittany Lions today. Still, this may be something that the Nittany Lions will want to look into ahead of next week.

This unit truly can do no wrong at the start of the season. They still have not yet allowed a passing touchdown, and while they gave up a late touchdown today, that's only the second one they've given up all year long. The fact they were flying all over the field and forcing two fumbles showcases the true potential of what this unit can be. Kooper Ebel especially impressed in the middle of the park today, leading the team in tackles and recording his first sack as a Nittany Lion. Overall, the defense should be mighty pleased with itself.

When the kickers do their job in a blowout, you have to commend them. Ryan Barker made two field goals and all six of his extra points, while Nathan Tiyce averaged 40.5 yards per punt with a long of 45. However, the star was Zay Robinson , who had 8 returns for 109 yards and really flashed potential in that role

The fact that Matt Campbell continues to get the most out of this team even in the early portion of their schedule is great. But now comes the hard part. In fact, the real grade will come with how he reacts to this win as he transitions to Big Ten play. He will be unsatisfied with several small details and will surely look to fix them, but for now, he has passed every test that has been thrown at him so far.

Penn State fans will be happy with yet another runaway victory for the blue and white, especially with an improved rushing attack and a high-flying defense. Now comes the real test of this Nittany Lion team's mettle. Can they truly compete with the best the Big Ten has to offer? Or will they, like previous iterations, become paper tigers when it matters most?

Penn State will be back in action next Saturday, September 26 when they start their Big Ten schedule against the Wisconsin Badgers at home. Kickoff is set for 5:00 ET on Peacock .

articles.title: 3 keys to victory for the Broncos against the Jaguars
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos need to follow these three keys to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2.
articles.body:
Last December, the Denver Broncos had won 11 games in a row. Then the Jacksonville Jaguars came to Denver and dealt them a 34-20 loss.

The loss temporarily threw the Broncos off their playoff track, but the team ultimately did enough to become the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Despite a near trip to Super Bowl LX, the Broncos have not forgotten that loss to the Jaguars, or the words from their coach , Liam Coen, that followed.

The Broncos will be looking to get a measure of revenge on Sunday while simultaneously bouncing back from an ugly loss to the Kansas City Chiefs last Monday night. That makes this a big early-season game for the Broncos and to finish on the right side of the result, these three factors will be key.

3 keys to victory for Broncos vs. Jaguars in Week 2

In order for the Broncos to be successful against Jacksonville, they'll need to immediately clean up what they could not do against Kansas City.

The Chiefs rushed for 220 yards on Monday night, including a career-high 173 from Kenneth Walker . That can't come even close to happening in this game. Much of that was due to the Broncos putting forth perhaps the worst tackling performance in league history.

Denver will need to be much better and much more disciplined in this game. That starts with coming out with much more energy than they did on Monday and using the home crowd to set the tone in this game.

The Jaguars are going to want to work the middle of the field against Denver's defense, using slot receiver Parker Washington to make big plays in the passing game. Against the Broncos last December, Washington posted 145 yards and a touchdown on six catches.

Ja'Quan McMillian will need to do what he can to limit Washington's playmaking ability and force Trevor Lawrence to try and throw to the boundaries, where Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss will be matched up against the duo of Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers . PS2 will take one of those guys out of the game and the Broncos should be willing to take their chances with Moss against the other.

Bo Nix had his first pass attempt of the season intercepted by the Chiefs. Aside from the ensuing drive after the Chiefs' first score, Nix had an incredibly bad game, arguably the worst of his young NFL career.

Davis Webb needs to look to get Nix going quickly in this game, setting up some easy throws for him in order to get him into a nice rhythm before taking some shots against a Jacksonville defense that can be susceptible to giving up some big plays.

articles.title: No. 3 St. Joseph shuts down defending Class MM champ Windsor behind Daniels, defense
articles.summary: St. Joseph scored on all five of its first-half possessions while holding Windsor to just two first downs.
articles.body:
TRUMBULL - Justin Daniels is just two games deep into his time with the St. Joseph football team. Judging by the results on the field, it's been an ideal match.

Daniels scored three touchdowns, running back Michael Charland added two and the defense pitched a shutout when No. 3 St. Joseph overwhelmed defending Class MM champion Windsor 43-0 in a Connecticut High School Football Alliance game on Saturday at St. Joseph.

The Hogs were on point from the start, jumping out to a 36-point lead in the first half and putting the game into running time for the final three quarters.

"We knew from the jump that if we started fast, we played physical and we played our brand of football, that we'd come out on top," said Daniels, a transfer from McMahon. "That's what we did for all four quarters from the first whistle to the last."

It was about as perfect a first half as the Hogs could have hoped for. They scored at least a field goal on each of their first five possessions, and were in destroyer mode on defense, holding Windsor to 27 yards in the first half. Windsor had two first downs before halftime, with one coming on a pass interference penalty.

"Our keys started with the defense," said senior Jake Rios. "If we shut them out, we knew we'd score. We knew we had to come out stronger than we did last week. The way we came out today and just drove down the field and score, score, score, with no punts on the day, that carried us through the whole game."

While St. Joseph is now 2-0 and ranked third in the GametimeCT Top 10 poll , Windsor has dropped to 0-2, the first time since 1997 that the Warriors have started a season with two losses. The defeats have come against top playoff contenders in New Britain and St. Joseph.

The Warriors are the defending Class MM champs, but have had a few changes, including the graduation of GametimeCT Player of the Year quarterback AJ Robinson and the transfer of All-State receiver Missoni Brown. Another All-State wide receiver, Jayden Compton, is back, but he left Saturday's game after a hard hit in the second half.

Windsor coach Rob Fleeting said the frustration comes because the Warriors have the talent in place and haven't put it together through the first two weeks.

"I'm disappointed because, if we weren't capable, I'd say 'we're just young,' but we're capable. We're big up front. We're just not getting the job done and that's frustrating," Fleeting said. "We've got to sit down and really assess where the growth is."

Leading 20-0 early in the second quarter, the Hogs put the game out of reach thanks to some trouble on punts for the Warriors.

Paul Karafa deflected a punt, which gave St. Joseph a short field and led to a touchdown. On Windsor's next punt attempt, the ball was snapped into the end zone, and Karafa made the tackle for a safety.

Daniels then returned the ensuing free kick for a touchdown.

articles.title: "Take that cross off your neck": Fans trash Sophie Cunningham over Sydney Sweeney comments as WNBA debate intensifies
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham has weighed in on Sydney Sweeney’s controversial sports betting ad, but the reaction online has become a story of its own. While the.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has weighed in on Sydney Sweeney’s controversial sports betting ad, but the reaction online has become a story of its own. While the Indiana Fever guard questioned the campaign’s authenticity and raised concerns about its message, some fans rushed to defend Sweeney. Others turned the discussion into a debate about women in sports, beauty standards and why the ad drew so much attention.Sophie Cunningham questions Sydney Sweeney’s controversial adCunningham shared her thoughts on Sweeney’s Novig campaign during the premiere of her revamped podcast, No Hesitation, which she co-hosts with Drew Hanlen. The ad features Sweeney appearing nude while trying different sports and repeating the phrase, “Just sports.”Cunningham questioned whether Sweeney genuinely follows sports betting and described the campaign as inauthentic. Still, she made it clear that her criticism of the ad did not mean she disliked the actress.“I have so many takes,” Cunningham said. “First of all, like, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it’s just so inauthentic. You know what I mean? Am I surprised of how she represented the brand? No. That’s what she’s made her whole career off — and, hey, don’t get me wrong. I like her. Everyone knows she is beautiful; she is hot. She clearly has my chest.”Cunningham also acknowledged Sweeney’s right to make her own choices, adding, “I really like her,” before explaining that the campaign was not to her taste.Hanlen suggested Sweeney was following a familiar marketing approach, pointing to her previous American Eagle campaign. Cunningham then questioned why women were particularly upset, given that the ad appeared to target men.“But why are girls mad?” Cunningham said. “That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad. Men, sports, pretty much naked women. Like, of course, that’s gonna draw attention. Again, do I agree with it? Morally, I think it’s kind of weird, but to each their own. Go do your thing, sis.”She later stressed that she did not believe the campaign was intended to undermine women in sports. Cunningham also praised athletes who challenge traditional beauty standards and encourage young girls to embrace their bodies.Sophie Cunningham’s comments spark divided fan reactionsCunningham’s take quickly became a talking point online, with fans split over whether Sweeney’s ad deserved criticism or was simply another marketing campaign.One commenter argued that the ad was simply doing what sports betting promotions are designed to do, writing, “It’s a sports betting ad look at it for what it is. No different that beer ads or hooters girls and chicken. Its has nothing to do with Women sports”Another added, "Sophie, please take that cross off your neck. I know exactly what you’re, nothing but a puppet for the elite. You stand for absolutely nothing and believe that God made you tall so you could play basketball. Full blown hypocrite."Another fan suggested jealousy was driving the backlash, claiming, “The ones that are mad are just jealous. That's all. It is just like all the women in the WNBA. It's pure jealousy. They don't know how to handle it and so they act like children”Others took a more provocative approach. One user wrote, “Threesome with Cunningham and Sweeney would be the ultimate dream,” while another commented, “Sidney is hotter than fish grease. She can’t help herself.”Some reactions focused on the campaign’s political and cultural implications. One commenter wrote, “Because she’s white. If she was black nobody would complain. Weird agenda type shit”Another fan suggested a joint campaign featuring both women, posting, “Now do an ad with Sophie AND Sydney in it together! The libal lefts heads will explode like in that movie Scanners 🤣🤣🤣🤣”Not every response focused on the controversy. One user questioned the promotion itself, writing, “Why is nobody talking about the $25 credit? It's sad. $200 in the average.”The comments show how Cunningham’s remarks have sparked a broader online argument about advertising, women in sports and public reactions to Sweeney’s campaign. While fans remain divided, the debate has pushed the Novig ad far beyond its original sports betting pitch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Victoria Beckham and David Beckham bought an 11,500-sq-ft Beverly Hills villa for $22 million; after 11 years, it sold for $33 million in an off-market deal
articles.summary: International Sports News: David and Victoria Beckham’s Beverly Hills mansion sold for about $33.1 million in 2018, ending an 11-year run at the California home. The couple had .
articles.body: David and Victoria Beckham’s Beverly Hills mansion sold for about $33.1 million in 2018, ending an 11-year run at the California home. The couple had bought the Italian-style villa in 2007, around the time David Beckham moved to the US to play for LA Galaxy. Property records and reports put their purchase price at about $18.2 million, meaning the sale brought them nearly $15 million more before taxes, fees and other costs. The deal was completed off-market, with the buyer listed through a limited liability company, keeping the new owner’s identity private.How much did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham pay for their Beverly Hills homeDavid Beckham and Victoria Beckham bought the Beverly Hills property in 2007 after David moved to Los Angeles to begin his Major League Soccer career with LA Galaxy. The home was an Italian villa-style property tucked away behind large gates and a private drive.The purchase price is one area where different reports have given different numbers. The Los Angeles Times reported that the Beckhams paid $18.2 million for the house. Other websites have since repeated a $22 million figure, but the $18.2 million figure is the one backed by the 2018 property reporting from the Los Angeles Times.The house gave the family a private base in Los Angeles while David played in the US. Victoria Beckham was also building her career outside football, first through fashion and later through her own clothing label.The property had about 11,500 to more than 13,000 square feet of living space, depending on the source. It had six bedrooms, multiple living areas, a library, an elevator and a media and music room. The house was also surrounded by gates and landscaping that gave the family a high level of privacy.What did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham’s Beverly Hills villa includeThe size of the home was only part of what made it notable. Its layout was designed for a large family and for entertaining, with several rooms spread across the property.The villa had six bedrooms and about nine to 10 bathrooms, with reports differing slightly on the exact bathroom count. There was also a library, a media and music room, formal living and dining spaces and an elevator.Outside, the property had a swimming pool and large private grounds. Its position behind iron gates and at the end of a private drive meant visitors could not simply see the house from the street.The home also became closely linked with the Beckham family’s years in Los Angeles. Their children lived there during the family’s time in the city, while David continued his football career and Victoria worked on her growing fashion business.The house was not simply a short-term stop after David’s move to the US. The couple kept it for more than a decade, even after David’s playing career in Los Angeles had ended.Why did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham sell the Beverly Hills mansionBy the time the house was sold, the family’s life had changed considerably. David Beckham retired from professional football in 2013, while Victoria Beckham’s fashion business had become an increasingly important part of her career in London.The family also had a growing connection to the UK, where they had a home in Holland Park and a country property in the Cotswolds. Their children were also spending more of their time in Britain.David’s business interests later brought the family closer to Miami. He became a co-owner of Inter Miami CF, giving him another major reason to spend time in South Florida.That made the Beverly Hills property less central to the family’s life. Instead of putting it through a traditional public listing, the Beckhams sold it privately.The Los Angeles Times reported in October 2018 that the house had been sold off-market for about $33.1 million. The buyer appeared in property records through a limited liability company, so the identity of the person or people behind the purchase was not publicly disclosed.The private sale also meant there was no long public listing process for the house. The deal was completed in September 2018, after the Beckhams had owned the property for about 11 years.How much profit did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham make from the Beverly Hills saleUsing the reported $18.2 million purchase price and the roughly $33.1 million sale price, the Beckhams made about $14.9 million in gross profit on the property before transaction costs, taxes, renovations and other expenses.The sale therefore represented a rise of roughly 82% in the property’s price over the 11-year holding period, although that does not mean the couple took home the full increase as profit.Mansion Global also reported that the home had been quietly shopped around before the eventual transaction and confirmed that it was sold without being publicly listed. The buyer was recorded as a Delaware limited liability company.The Beverly Hills sale also fits into a wider change in the Beckhams’ US property interests. In 2020, David and Victoria bought a full-floor residence at Miami’s One Thousand Museum for $19.8 million. The Zaha Hadid-designed tower became part of their South Florida property holdings during David’s growing involvement with Inter Miami.That Miami apartment was later sold for about $24.6 million in 2026, according to property reporting. The couple also bought a waterfront Miami Beach mansion in 2024 for about $72.3 million, below its $80 million asking price.So, while the Beverly Hills home is now part of the Beckhams’ past property portfolio, its sale marked an important point in the family’s move away from their old Los Angeles base and toward a stronger connection with Miami.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 4: Arjun Erigaisi picks first win of tournament; India's winning juggernaut rolls on
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad began on a murky note, with multiple teams facing accommodation issues upon arrival in host city Sam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad began on a murky note, with multiple teams facing accommodation issues upon arrival in host city Samarkand, Uzbekistan. India, the defending champions across both the open and women's sections, also had to wait for hours before players were allotted separate rooms. Coming off a gruelling week back home for the Global Chess League (GCL), one of the players who had to hop straight from the Bengaluru event to Samarkand was India's No. 2 Arjun Erigaisi.When Praggnanandhaa opted to rest for the opening-day fixture against Thailand, it was Arjun who stepped in to play Board 1. Playing white, he lost to Thailand's 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap.World champion Gukesh, who has had a commendable score of 3.5/4 in this tournament, explained what had gone wrong for Arjun. "Arjun's first game was very unfortunate, but also worth mentioning that we had very hectic travel and then the first day there were some organisation issues," Gukesh said in an interview with FIDE after his Round 3 win over Italy's Sabino Brunello. "So, Arjun got a room probably a few hours before he went. I mean, we all waited for like six hours to get a room. So obviously, in the first round, Arjun was just tired, and he blundered in the end."Gukesh added that things had improved since then. "The first day was a bit tricky for all of us, but after that, I think we are all rested. We are all looking forward to the games and all good," he said.Those words showed up in the results on Saturday, when Arjun took down Maksim Chigaev to secure his first win of the tournament, helping India beat Spain 3-1.How Arjun Erigaisi won his first game at the 2026 Chess OlympiadArjun Erigaisi, playing white, produced a controlled attacking performance against Maksim Chigaev.The opening was a flexible Réti/English setup, with White gaining space through 12.h4 and 13.h5, provoking ...g5 and creating long-term kingside targets.After 14.d5, White secured a useful space advantage while Black’s pieces became somewhat passive.The key strategic phase began with 17.Nh2 and 18.Bh3, followed by the exchange of bishops on c8. Erigaisi then expanded with 21.e4 and 23.f4, correctly opening lines while Black’s king remained vulnerable.The sequence 28.Qe4 Rxf1 29.Rxf1 Rf8 30.Rxf8+ simplified the rooks and left White with a dangerous queen-and-knight attack.The decisive phase was 31.Qh7, followed by 32.Qh8+ and 33.Ng4, coordinating queen and knight around the exposed king. After 34.Nxe5+, Black could not escape the perpetual-looking checks, and 36.Qf7+ ended the game.Elsewhere on the board, Gukesh continued his fine run, beating Spain's Alexei Shirov to move to 4.5/5 and continuing a solid turnaround from Thursday's dip below the 2700 rating mark.Praggnanandhaa and Nihal Sarin both drew their games, enough for India to close out the tie 3-1.For Erigaisi specifically, the win carries added significance. As India's second-highest rated player and a regular on Board 1 or 2 duty, a winless start would have added pressure to an already long season that had him travelling directly from the GCL in Bengaluru to Samarkand with barely any time to recover. Saturday's result suggests that adjustment period may now be behind him.India's winning juggernaut marches onIndia's women's team also kept their unbeaten run alive, beating Mongolia 3-1. Koneru Humpy and Vaishali Rameshbabu both drew their games against lower-rated opposition.But Divya Deshmukh and Savitha Shri won on the lower boards to see the team through comfortably, continuing a campaign that has yet to drop a match tie.With both squads now through four rounds without a defeat as a team, the tests only get tougher from here. India will take on Poland in the women's section on Sunday, while the open team faces a mouthwatering clash against Anish Giri's Dutch side, arguably the sternest test either Indian team has faced so far in Samarkand.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Young kids and young fans that were super excited”: Caitlin Clark reveals best thing about international games during her FIBA run with Team USA
articles.summary: International Sports News: Caitlin Clark came back from Berlin with a gold medal and a new idea about where the WNBA should play. In a candid chat, Clark shared it on Friday, af.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark came back from Berlin with a gold medal and a new idea about where the WNBA should play. In a candid chat, Clark shared it on Friday, after the Fever beat the Toronto Tempo.The Indiana Fever superstar has a clear favorite memory from the trip, and it has nothing to do with the trophy. It is about the people who came out to watch Team USA play in Europe. The league, meanwhile, has been thinking along the same lines, with international games planned as soon as the 2027 regular season.What Caitlin Clark took away from the FIBA World Cup in BerlinFreshly back from Berlin, Caitlin Clark spoke to reporters on Friday after the Fever beat the Toronto Tempo. Team USA had won its sixth straight FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gold there, and Clark helped get the team over the line. The talk, though, went well past the medal.One of the biggest takeaways for Clark was the pride. Players from other countries, especially those who play in the WNBA and return to suit up for home, take the job seriously. “So it was really fun for myself to play international basketball and I think one of the biggest things I took away is how much pride those girls play with,” Clark shared. It means a great deal to them. Clark called it really cool and pointed to how much those players have done to grow the game in their own countries.Europe added a memory of its own. Playing there felt amazing, and the crowds made it better. Clark said the number of "young kids and young fans that were super excited" to see Team USA stood out.The sport has only scratched the surface of its reach around the world, and a WNBA game overseas next year would not surprise Clark. As for playing in one, Clark is all in. Helping the league expand sounds good, and Clark is looking forward to it.Caitlin Clark's wish and the WNBA's plan for games abroadThe wish may not stay a wish for long. Outgoing WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert has said the league plans to bring in international games as soon as the 2027 regular season. Engelbert will not be around beyond this season, but whoever takes the job is expected to carry the plan forward.The WNBA has little history abroad to build on. Before the Toronto Tempo joined as an expansion team in 2026, the league had played only one regular season game outside the United States. The Atlanta Dream and Seattle Storm played it last season in Vancouver, British Columbia, on Aug. 15, 2025.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Quimcy Dsouza's Asian Games campaign ended in heartbreaking fashion as the Indian teqball player went down 0-2 to Japan's world No. 7 Yuina Sakamoto in the women's singles bronze medal match here on Saturday.Despite the straight-set defeat, the 11-12, 11-12 scoreline hardly reflects how close the Mumbai player came to claiming the bronze. With a partisan home crowd backing Sakamoto, Dsouza pushed the Japanese star all the way in both sets, only to miss out by the narrowest of margins.The Indian had a set point in the opening game but could not convert it. She then appeared to be on course to force a decider after racing into a 10-8 advantage in the second set.Sakamoto, however, fought back to earn match point. Dsouza refused to go down without a fight, saving it with a winner to keep her hopes alive. But her comeback ended moments later when she committed a foul, handing Sakamoto the point needed to close out the match.Women's singles teqball follows a best-of-three format, with the first player to win two sets advancing. A set is won by the first player to reach 12 points. In the opening two sets, a one-point margin is enough, while a deciding third set requires a player to establish a two-point advantage.For Dsouza, the bronze-medal defeat capped a dramatic Asian Games debut. She had already stunned Sakamoto in the group stage, defeating the Japanese world No. 7 before eventually meeting her again with a medal at stake.Teqball, which made its Asian Games debut at the 20th edition of the continental event, is a non-contact sport combining elements of football and table tennis. Players rally a standard football across a specially curved table resembling a table tennis table, using any part of their body except their hands and arms. articles.title: Denied by visa row in 2023, former Asia No. 1 Rupa Bayor finally gets her Games shot
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: KOLKATA: When Rupa Bayor qualified for the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, the taekwondo poomsae specialist from Arunachal Pradesh believed she had a ge.
articles.body: KOLKATA: When Rupa Bayor qualified for the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, the taekwondo poomsae specialist from Arunachal Pradesh believed she had a genuine shot at finishing on the podium.Instead, she watched from afar after being denied the opportunity to compete because of the visa issue involving athletes from Arunachal Pradesh.“It was very painful at the time because I felt I had a genuine chance of winning a medal,” Rupa told TOI in an exclusive interaction. “But some things are beyond your control. Eventually, you have to move forward and focus on the future.”Three years later, the 26-year-old gets her long-awaited Asiad debut as one of India’s medal hopes in taekwondo poomsae after a remarkable rise that saw her become the first Indian poomsae athlete to reach Asia No. 1 and a career-high world No. 5 earlier this year, although she is currently ranked second in Asia and seventh in the world.Her coach, Abhishek Dubey, believes the disappointment of missing the previous Games ultimately made her stronger.“At that time, she was already among the top-ranked athletes in Asia and we felt she had a genuine chance of winning a medal,” said Dubey, who has been involved in the sport for around 36 years as a coach, administrator and sports management professional.“An athlete’s career is short and the Asian Games come only once every four years. It was extremely disappointing, but we decided to stay focused and continue training. Fortunately, we managed to do that and now we are in a position where we genuinely believe a medal is possible.”The journey to this point, however, has been anything but conventional.Raised in the Daporijo area of Arunachal’s Upper Subansiri district, Rupa was introduced to combat sports by her maternal uncle, Tabu Sera, who practised karate. Back then, international competitions felt impossibly distant.“At the grassroots level, the Asian Games felt like a distant dream,” she recalled. “We didn’t have international athletes around us, so our mindset was simply to participate in competitions and come back home.”Behind Rupa’s rise also lies a story of resilience. She lost her father at a very young age and was raised by her mother, a farmer who supported the family in rural Arunachal. Growing up far from India’s sporting centres, the odds of reaching an event like the Asian Games seemed remote.But everything changed in 2021 when she moved to Navi Mumbai to train under Dubey.“I was looking for a good place to train for a long time,” she said. “When I saw the athletes he was coaching and the results they were achieving, I felt he was the right coach for me.”Dubey still remembers the day she arrived in Mumbai. “She just landed up with her bags and wanted to train,” he said. “What stood out immediately was her competitiveness and willingness to learn.”That discipline has translated into results. Rupa has won medals consistently on the international circuit and defeated several best athletes of Asia, including competitors who medalled at the previous Asian Games.This year, she won bronze at the Asian Taekwondo Poomsae Championships in Ulaanbaatar, becoming the first Indian athlete to win medals in two consecutive editions of the continental event.The dream that once seemed out of reach is thus now within touching distance. And after spending three years waiting for a chance that was taken away from her, Rupa, currently in South Korea for the 2026 World Taekwondo Poomsae Championships, has only one goal in mind.“My mindset is no longer about just participating,” she said. “Whenever I compete, I want to win a medal.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India's Suraj Singh Mayanglambam finished 11th in the men's Changquan Wushu final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday, ending his campaign outside the medal positions after competing in a 21-athlete field.Performing at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall, Suraj registered an overall score of 9.683 points. articles.title: On Games debut, shuttler Isharani Baruah ‘ready’ to challenge Asian powerhouses
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: When Isharani Baruah looks at India’s badminton squad for the Asian Games, she doesn’t see a team overawed by Asia’s traditional powerhouse.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Isharani Baruah looks at India’s badminton squad for the Asian Games, she doesn’t see a team overawed by Asia’s traditional powerhouses.The 22-year-old from Assam will make her Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya, stepping into a squad that brings together the experience of two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu and the emergence of youngsters such as Tanvi Sharma, Unnati Hooda and the doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand.For Isharani, the journey to this stage began almost by accident. Growing up in Dibrugarh, she was a regular fixture among the boys playing different kinds of sport in her neighbourhood. A neighbour noticed her enthusiasm and suggested badminton to her mother. There was no sporting pedigree at home, no elaborate plan for a career in badminton — just a young girl, a racquet and an opportunity that changed the course of her life.India’s medal ambitions in Aichi-Nagoya come against a backdrop of steady progress on the Asian circuit. The gap with China, Japan and other established powers may still exist, but Indian players are increasingly finding themselves on the latter stages of tournaments rather than merely entering them.For Isharani, the evidence is there week after week.“If you see the Super 100 and Super 300 tournaments, there are always three or four Indians reaching the quarterfinals or semifinals. Even in the 500s, we’re competing well. Badminton has definitely grown in India, and we’re going to reach the level of countries like China and Japan quite soon. We’re ready to challenge these powerhouses at the Asian Games,” she said.Her own rise has followed that same route. Consistent performances on the lower-tier circuit have helped her climb the rankings and, more importantly, exposed her to opponents from the badminton-heavy nations of Asia.“To reach the Super 750 and 1000 events, you first have to perform in the 100s and 300s because that’s how you earn ranking points. Playing against Chinese and Japanese opponents there and beating them gives us confidence before the bigger tournaments,” Isharani said.But perhaps the biggest change in her game has not been technical. It has been between the ears. Once prone to tightening up after mistakes, Isharani has learned to treat composure as part of her game plan. The smile that often appears on court is not simply an expression of enjoyment; it has become a way of resetting herself.“For me, the most important thing is to enjoy playing. Even if I’m making mistakes, I don’t want to become tense because then I lose focus on the next point. I keep smiling, I talk to my coaches more, and I trust the process,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games: Several Indian athletes await ceremonial kits, Tajinderpal Singh Toor episode raises questions
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA/NEW DELHI: If the first controversy involving the Indian contingent at the Asian Games was expected to take time to surface, it did not. It cam.
articles.body: NAGOYA/NEW DELHI: If the first controversy involving the Indian contingent at the Asian Games was expected to take time to surface, it did not. It came less than 24 hours before the opening ceremony.In a last-minute change in Nagoya on Friday night, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) replaced defending shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor with kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat as the Indian flagbearer alongside Manu Bhaker for Saturday’s opening ceremony.The dramatic turn of events unfolded after Toor, who had earlier spoken of his pride at being named flagbearer, realised that he did not have the ceremonial kit required for the opening and closing ceremonies.All athletes are provided the ceremonial kit as part of their Games kit, irrespective of whether they attend the opening ceremony. So what went wrong?TOI understands that prior to departure for the Games, Toor had received a ceremonial kit in the wrong size, which was sent back for alteration. The altered kit, however, did not reach him before his departure.Toor trained at the National Institute of Sports in Patiala before joining the track and field contingent in New Delhi for the official send-off and Indian Athletics Finals Series on September 10. He then travelled to the University of Tsukuba for the pre-Games training camp.Sources said the issue came to a head on Friday night, with the ceremonial kit still unavailable in Nagoya. Toor was quoted as saying he had informed the IOA that he would be unable to attend the ceremony as the kit was not expected to reach him before 3pm on Saturday — three hours before the ceremony.The IOA initially attributed the replacement to “technical” reasons. Toor was also initially said to have forgotten to carry his ceremonial kit, a version that he subsequently disputed.“Looks like he has been told to say that he forgot to carry his kit in India when he had received none,” a source alleged.It has since emerged that the issue was more complicated, with several athletes yet to receive their ceremonial kits.“There was miscommunication between the athlete, AFI and IOA on the issue. If the athlete is carrying with him his playing and training kits from India, he should also pack the ceremonial kit,” a source said.Sources said the IOA contingent staff in Aichi-Nagoya should have checked with the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) whether its athletes had received their ceremonial kits before announcing Toor’s name. Likewise, the AFI should have confirmed with the athlete before forwarding his name.The issue was compounded by the fact that more than 100 Indian athletes were reportedly yet to receive their ceremonial kits. With the contingent expanding and last-minute requirements having to be met from the available stock, officials were racing against time.Toor, who is set to defend his shot put title, eventually took responsibility publicly for the episode. But the last-minute replacement exposed a communication gap between the athlete, federation and IOA — and raised questions over the coordination.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Caitlin Clark has found another way to help children away from the basketball court. On May 15, 2026, the Caitlin Clark Foundation announced a $50,000 donation to Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital at Ascension St. Vincent in Indianapolis. The gift supports children and families during hospital stays, with the money going towards Child Life Services.The donation also has a personal connection to Clark’s community. Her foundation focuses on helping young people learn, grow and thrive, and this gift puts that mission into action for children facing difficult days in hospital. Caitlin Clark puts $50,000 behind care for young patientsThe Caitlin Clark Foundation announced the donation on May 15, 2026. Later that month, Clark’s mother, Anne Nizzi-Clark, visited Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital on behalf of the foundation to present the gift and spend time with people connected to the hospital’s work.The $50,000 supports Child Life Services, a programme that helps young patients deal with the stress and challenges that can come with being in hospital. Certified Child Life Specialists work with children and their families through education, play, distraction, relaxation and emotional support.That can make a difference during a hospital stay, when a child’s normal routine can suddenly disappear. The programme gives children ways to understand what is happening around them and offers families additional support as they navigate treatment.Clark explained the reason behind the gift in the foundation’s May 15 announcement.“Supporting children and families has always been at the heart of the Foundation. I’m grateful for the opportunity to support Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital at Ascension St. Vincent and the important work they do for patients and families in Indianapolis,” Clark said in the foundation’s announcement about the donation.The foundation later highlighted the same donation in a June 2026 social media post, saying the gift went specifically to Child Life Services at the Indianapolis hospital. Caitlin Clark’s work with kids goes well beyond the basketball courtThe Indianapolis donation fits into a larger focus for the Caitlin Clark Foundation. Its stated mission centres on education, nutrition and sports, with the goal of creating opportunities for young people and their communities.The foundation has also backed children's hospitals in Iowa this year. On April 24, 2026, it announced a $22,000 grant to University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children’s Hospital. On May 6, it announced another $22,000 grant for Blank Children’s Hospital in Des Moines.Clark also spoke about the Iowa City donation, saying, “I’m a big believer that the right support at the right time can change the trajectory of a person’s day, and sometimes even their future.” She made that comment in the foundation’s April 24 announcement.The $50,000 Indianapolis gift follows that same idea.
