articles.title: Japan opens Asian Games 2026 with a heartfelt celebration of culture and unity in Aichi-Nagoya
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: Almost three hours before the start of the Asian Games opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, spectators had begun filling the .
articles.body: NAGOYA: Almost three hours before the start of the Asian Games opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, spectators had begun filling the expansive, multi-tiered stands. The 35,000-capacity venue was not full, but that did little to dampen the celebration that followed.The first glimpse was of a gigantic heart. But this was not merely about love. The heart-shaped stage, bathed in white, underlined the ceremony’s theme — Harmonic Hea-rtbeat. Like matcha, sake or sushi, themes and cultures can be an acquired taste. Whi-le some found the nearly two-hour spectacle underwhelming, from a Japanese perspective it was a celebration steeped in tradition, culture, diversity and technology.The evening began with a pre-ceremony performance by the Shigo Bonote Preservation Society and the hugely popular INI boy band. The ceremony itself opened with dancers in heart-shaped attire and a performance by celebrated Japanese violinist Taro Hakase. With Japanese royalty led by emperor Naruhito and empress Masako, International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry and Olympic Council of Asia president Sheikh Joaan Hamad Al Thani among the dignitaries in attendance, the Japanese national flag was raised by members of the Japan Self-Defence Forces.Volunteers carrying heart-shaped placards bearing the names of participating countries then led the athletes and officials into the stadium. The Indians, looking dapper in deep blue, received a warm welcome, though the loudest cheers in the stadium were reserved for the hosts.The centrepiece of the night was a replica of Nagoya Castle, placed at the heart of the stage and illuminated in a kaleidoscope of colours.The heart-shaped cauldron was lit by five-time Asian Games champion and hammer throw legend Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji, the 2004 Olympic hammer throw champion.Sheikh Joaan in his speech said, “Tonight, the eyes of Asia and much of the world turn to Japan. What we will see over the next few days will inspire us. It will move us. And it will remind us of what we are capable of when we come together for Asia.”With One Asia, One Heart at the centre of the ceremony, the troubles of the past few days, which had put Nagoya’s ability to host the Games under scrutiny, seemed to fade into the background, at least for the night.The ceremony ended with fireworks lighting up the night sky, offering a fitting hope that the Games, too, will shine as brightly.Who will open India’s medal tally?India, who returned from the 2022 Hangzhou Games with a record 107 medals, will begin their quest to better that haul on Sunday, with three disciplines offering early opportunities to get on the board.All eyes will be on the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Ra-nge, with India expected to be in the thick of action, fighting for a podium finish. Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod will comp-ete in the women’s 10m air rif-le, with medals at stake in bo-th the team and individual ev-ents. In women’s cricket, defe-nding champions India face Bangladesh in the semifinal. A win will assure India of a m-edal. There could also be an interesting twist to India’s medal-opening narrative. In teqball, two bronze medals are up for grabs, while Suraj Singh will compete in the men’s changquan event, a medal event on the day, in wushu.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch Ryan Blaney, Carson Hocevar Throw Punches in Fight After Crash at Bristol During NASCAR Chase
articles.summary: NASCAR drivers Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar were involved in a physical altercation following a crash during Saturday's night race at Bristol Motor Speedway.
articles.body:
NASCAR drivers Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar were involved in a physical altercation following a crash during Saturday's night race at Bristol Motor Speedway.

With 43 laps remaining in the race, Blaney's No. 12 Ford spun after making contact with Hocevar's No. 77 Chevrolet.

Blaney confronted Hocevar on pit road afterwards, as the two drivers ended up exchanging punches.

"Something's gonna happen…tonight," Blaney told reporters regarding the incident.

Blaney led for 202 laps prior to the crash, winning Stage 1 and Stage 2 before he was unable to finish.

Hocevar completed the race in the No. 3 spot, as Joey Logano ended up winning.

Blaney sits at No. 6 in the NASCAR Cup Series standings , while Hocevar holds the No. 8 position. Both drivers are in The Chase, competing in a 10-race championship battle.

Hocevar's driving style has led to tension with others in the past, as the 23-year-old was previously called out by Brad Keselowski after he was sent for a full spin during the Cook Out Southern 500 at Darlington Raceway on Sept. 6.

Now, Hocevar is involved in a feud with Blaney.

articles.title: Highlights! Pitbull Cruz Knocks Out Bravo, Calls Out Ryan Garcia
articles.summary: Patricio Pitbull wasn’t the only one with that moniker who secured a massive knockout win last night (Sat., Sept, 19, 2026), as Pitbull Cruz locked one down...
articles.body:
Patricio Pitbull wasn't the only one with that moniker who secured a massive knockout win last night (Sat., Sept, 19, 2026), as Pitbull Cruz locked one down himself a few hours later in his WBC Super Lightweight title fight against Nestor Bravo in San Diego, California.

Cruz and Bravo had a lot of tension coming into the fight, though it was Cruz who was getting the better of the exchanges once the action got started, knocking him down in the very first round. But it got a bit sloppy at times, with referee Thomas Taylor having to constantly scold Bravo for holding a bit too much for his liking. Bravo was deducted a point on two occasions in the first four rounds alone for picking Pitbull up and slamming him to the canvas. Furthermore, the official even warned him that he was close to getting disqualified.

In round six, however, Cruz took it out of the referee and judges hands by tagging Bravo with a nasty left hook that dropped him to the canvas. Bravo never got back up to answer the 10 count, though we can't look past the fact that Taylor seemed to count a bit faster than usual.

Still, it was obvious Cruz was simply too much for Bravo, and even the commentators were accusing the challenger of simply looking for a way out of the fight with his dirty tactics.

Afterward, Cruz called out WBC Welterweight champion Ryan Garcia — who is fresh off a knockout win over Conor Benn — to a fight. Not one to sit idle without a response, Garcia accepted the challenge for an end-of-the-year showdown.

articles.title: As part of their tribute to Todd Helton, Rockies beat the Mariners 5-3
articles.summary: The Rockies come back from an early deficit with an exhilarating seventh inning barrage
articles.body:
Entering tonight with a taxed bullpen and a starting pitcher fresh off the injured list, the Colorado Rockies managed to battle back from an early deficit to earn a victory on a day of celebration for Todd Helton, a franchise legend.

Manager Warren Schaffer described the game as "one of my favorite wins of the season" in his post-game press conference, and it's not hard to see why he would feel that way as the Rockies bested the Seattle Mariners , 5-3.

José Quintana 's return to the mound started off looking very good.

He got both JP Crawford and Randy Arozarena to strike out swinging to begin the game. Dominic Canzone worked the count full before walking on a pitch right at the top of the zone that was close enough that it may have been turned into a strike had Hunter Goodman challenged it.

Instead, Canzone walked to first and was immediately driven in on Cal Raleigh 's 23rd home run of the season.

Quintana navigated through the second inning without allowing any additional runs, but it wasn't without drama. Michael Arroyo singled on a soft fly-ball blooper with one out. Lazaro Montes came up after Arroyo and grounded out on what may have been a double-play ball that unluckily deflected off of Quintana's foot. Connor Norby was able to adjust and salvage the play to get a single out at first but the inning continued.

The third inning featured Quintana allowing a home run by Randy Arozarena that would land in, essentially, the same spot that Raleigh's had in the first.

The Mariners weren't done with just that homer, however, and Canzone would immediately reach base on a soft single to left once Arozarena finished his trot around the bases. Quintana got Raleigh to pop up for the second out of the inning before Julio Rodriguez singled and advanced Canzone to third.

Josh Naylor then hit a hard liner to right center field that would have been at least a double if not for a very difficult running catch from Cole Carrigg that ended the inning.

Quintana came back out for the fourth and was able to set down the side on just an additional 14 pitches. The only hard contact was a liner from Montes that was caught on a good play by Rumfield at first.

Given his long stint on the injured list, Quintana was relieved before the fifth after having reached 70 pitches. He ended his return outing with four innings pitched with three runs (all earned) on five hits and a single walk.

Speaking to reporters after the game Quintana did not hold back on what being able to finish the year on the mound meant to him:

"It's huge for me. Especially when you have an elbow issue. I know the process I've been doing for a while and want to say thank you to the Colorado Rockies organization for giving me the chance to be back and waiting for me to be healthy. It was a long process and for me I just feel lucky and blessed to get this opportunity. I know how hard I've been working to be in this position right now but it's huge to finish strong, to finish pitching and enjoy this time with the team. I missed it for a long time."

The first couple innings of the game for the Rockies lineup were relatively quiet. Connor Norby hit a soft single in the first, and Kyle Karros managed a walk in the second, but the rest of the Rockies lineup was unable to drive either in.

Jake McCarthy got the Rockies on the board in the third inning by taking advantage of a series of rushed throws from the Mariners defense.

First, he hit a very soft ground ball that Mariners catcher Raleigh attempted to field on his own but missed the mark with his spinning throw to first that sent the ball sailing to right field, allowing McCarthy to reach third base safely.

Norby came to the plate and hit a sacrifice fly to shallow right field. The throw from Canzone went to the plate in an attempt to catch McCarthy, and it looked like it was going to before it hit the ground just in front of the awaiting Raleigh, who failed to block it.

McCarthy came in to score the Rockies first run of the game.

The next couple innings saw Mariners starter Bryce Miller settle in with the Rockies hitters unable to find an answer. A Zac Veen walk was the only Rockies baserunner throughout either of the fourth or fifth innings.

As the Rockies lineup got its third look at Miller in the sixth, however, they appeared to finally be figuring him out. Norby struck out to start the inning but was followed by hard ground singles from both TJ Rumfield and Hunter Goodman to produce only their second runner in scoring position to that point.

With the scoring threat established, Miller was relieved by Carlos Vargas after 89 pitches. Vargas went on to get Cole Carrigg to ground into a fielder's choice and induced a groundout from Karros to end the inning and the threat from the Rockies.

As deflating as the sixth inning felt at the time, it wouldn't take long before the Rockies would once again get some runners in scoring position. In the seventh inning, everything started to fall apart for the Mariners pitching.

It started off innocently enough with a Mickey Moniak lineout and an innocuous single from Veen. Adael Amador came in to pinch hit for Tovar, and the wheels started to come off for Mariners reliever Vargas.

During the Amador at-bat Vargas appeared notably pre-occupied with attempting to keep Veen at first who ultimately didn't attempt a steal. Amador, however, took the opportunity to smack a single of his own, and Vargas was pulled for Jose Ferrer.

Ferrer's outing lasted only four pitches.

McCarthy hit a sacrifice grounder that scored Veen. The inning should have ended the next batter after Norby hit a ground ball to third that was bobbled by Mariners third baseman Wilson. With the gifted extra out, Rumfield came to the plate and smacked an RBI single.

As Goodman and Carrigg prepared to hit, Mariners manager Dan Wilson puller Ferrer in favor of righty Cooper Criswell . Despite the platoon disadvantage, Goodman was able to work a walk that loaded the bases before Carrigg drove in the go-ahead runs on a single to shallow right center.

Karros walked the bases loaded again but the inning finally came to an end on a Moniak ground out to short. When the dust had settled on the seventh inning, the Rockies had scored four runs and were winning 5-3.

After Quintana exited following the fourth inning, Nick Frasso took over in the fifth to face the top of the Mariners lineup the third time through the order.

He induced a sharp lineout to third from Crawford before striking out Arozarena. Canzone worked a full count before Frasso walked him. Frasso didn't allow the long at bat and having a runner on first phase him, however, and managed to strike out Raleigh to end the inning the very next batter.

Rodriguez hit a double on a liner to left to open the sixth against Frasso. It soon looked like trouble after Naylor hit a popfly to advance Rodriguez to third. Then came a hard line drive towards left field by Arroyo . . . that was intercepted by a leaping Karros at third. Before Rodriguez had time to react, Karros tagged third and ended the inning on an unassisted double play.

Juan Mejia took over in the seventh and promptly produced the quietest two innings for Mariners hitters in the game to that point.

Other than a soft two-out double to left field from Raleigh in the eighth, Mejia shut down every hitter that came to the plate for two straight innings. After the game, Schaeffer heaped praise on Mejia's performance saying "Everyone knows that when he goes back out a second time that's been a struggle for him. Tonight he was nails. Not a pitch under 97."

It was an open quesiton as to who would take the ball in the ninth inning. According to manager Warren Schaeffer Jordan Romano was willing to pitch for a third day in a row but was "sick as a dog." So, instead, Schaeffer turned to another reliever that had pitched both of the previous two games: Brennan Bernardino .

Even though their usual closer wasn't available, the Rockies still took the opportunity to make a show of Bernardino entering for a save opportunity.

Benardino got Naylor to ground out to start the inning before Arroyo reached first on a fly ball to right. Bernardino ensured that the Mariners savior from Friday night would not repeat his ninth inning heroics for a second game in a row with a four-pitch strikeout of Montes.

A two-out strikeout from Wilson earned the Rockies their 57th win and Bernardino his third career save.

This electric win came as a fitting tribute to Colorado Rockies legend Todd Helton for whom a statue was unveiled before the game.

Helton was invited onto the field before the game for an additional honorary ceremony and threw out the first pitch to his daughter.

In the bottom of the third inning, Helton was invited into the Rockies television broadcast booth and talked about both the process of posing for the statue creation process joking that he "cramped up a little but" needing to hold his iconic pose for so long.

While Helton was watching McCarthy score the first Rockies run of the game, he spoke to his time on the 2007 Pennant-winning Rockies team and his celebration at catching the final out of the National League Championship series. About the fan response to that rare image of emotional response from him on the field Helton joked, "If I would have known it meant that much to people, I would've done it for 17 years. When you're winning, it's easy to be happy."

Given how happy the crowd in the stands at Coors Field sounded tonight watching the Rockies win, Helton may just be on to something.

Tomorrow night the Rockies will face the Mariners for the final time this season.

On the mound for the Rockies will be Tomoyuki Sugano facing Kade Anderson.

articles.title: Dodgers' September surge continues: L.A. racks up 15 hits in win over Giants
articles.summary: Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
articles.body:
When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense.

In the Dodgers ' 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies in back-to-back innings to take pressure off the pitching staff.

Before that breakout started in the fifth inning, it was a back-and-forth game.

Dodgers left-handed starting pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched only five innings, tied for his shortest start with the Dodgers. And he surrendered four runs, the worst mark of his Dodgers tenure.

Entering the game, Skubal appeared to be peaking. His past two starts, both against the Reds , were some of his most efficient.

That efficiency, however, regressed against the Giants (64-91).

Though he got through the first two innings without giving up a run — thanks in part to a diving catch by right fielder Kyle Tucker in the gap to end the first — he issued two-out walks in each.

The Dodgers' offense used that time to mount a lead. Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts , who finished the day with three doubles and a single, hit the first of those doubles in his first at-bat, and Max Muncy authored his own to drive in the first run.

The next inning, rookie Josue De Paula's walk, and singles from Alex Freeland and Betts combined to push in another run.

Then Skubal began to struggle. With a runner on second and one out, he pitched to a full count against designated hitter Victor Bericoto. Skubal missed down the middle with a fastball, and Bericoto sent it 425 feet to center field. It landed on the netting on the other side of the wall to tie the score.

The Dodgers' offense, coming alive in September, struck back in the third. Catcher Will Smith hit his second home run in as many nights, launching the second pitch of the inning into the left-field stands.

The Giants took a different approach to tie the score for a second time. After back-to-back singles, they used back-to-back sacrifice bunts to advance the runners and score another run.

Then the two teams traded runs again. Betts put the Dodgers (95-60) up with an RBI double in the fourth. Skubal gave up back-to-back doubles in the fifth.

That marked both the end of Skubal's start and the beginning of the Dodgers' offensive onslaught.

The Dodgers brought seven batters to the plate in the fifth, and all but one reached base. Tommy Edman hit a two-run single. And pinch-hitting Miguel Rojas almost matched him, but Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a perfect throw to nab Edman in a close play at home to end the inning.

Betts' and Smith's bats stayed hot to open the sixth with a leadoff double and one-out RBI single, respectively. The Dodgers took advantage of the Giants' sloppy infield play to load the bases for De Paula, who lined a two-run single into shallow center field.

Those were the kinds of stifling rallies that had defined the Dodgers' offense earlier in the season, when they were scoring regularly in double digits.

The Dodgers' 15 hits Saturday were their most in a game since July 2 against the San Diego Padres , and just two shy of their season high.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: LSU went all-in with Lane Kiffin circus. Then got served cold gumbo | Opinion
articles.summary: LSU built everything around Lane Kiffin. Then Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss delivered a painful reality check in Oxford.
articles.body:
There wasn't a moment since last December, not a single moment, where LSU didn't do everything possible to make it work.

Spent hundreds of millions of dollars, and mortgaged a financial and structural future. Fired a coach , and gave another an offer he couldn't refuse.

Gave him free reign over everything, and mimicked his every reckless lead .

Then the worst possible thing happened in the biggest moment of all. The Ole Miss game arrived, and LSU blinked.

That cold gumbo ? Tastes a lot like Ole Miss 32, LSU 24 .

It had to end this way, really. Had to wrap with Lane Kiffin, the man we love to hate yet secretly admire, skulking off the field he once made famous — with LSU a final drive shy of pulling off the damn thing.

Had to end with Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss — the one player Kiffin desperately wanted to join his band of modern day mercenaries, but couldn't get — leaping into the stands at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium with his fourth win at Ole Miss when tied or trailing in the fourth quarter.

Lane Kiffin returns to Oxford as LSU meets Ole Miss

Had to end with LSU getting off the deck after a 24-7 halftime deficit, and have the ball with a chance to tie the score and send it into overtime. A tipped ball interception officially ended it, but the pieces were in place long ago for this meltdown.

The worst possible thing that could happen to LSU on Saturday happened. Now what?

Now where does LSU go after pumping every ounce of energy and drama into Kiffin's triumphant return to Oxford, Miss., and the subsequent stroll of the conquering king that never materialized?

How does LSU now face a schedule that may be the toughest in the most difficult conference in college football? There's Alabama and Texas and Tennessee , and suddenly, Mississippi State and Kentucky don't look like pushovers anymore.

Star tight end Trey'Dez Green left the game in the fourth quarter with a lower body injury, and the offense quickly bogged down. The defense that looked unbreakable against Clemson and Louisiana Tech, couldn't get off the field — despite star Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy injuring his shoulder in the first half and never returning.

The $50 million roster built to not only win this game, but every other in the inevitable run to the greatest season in LSU history, has holes. Legit, problematic holes.

Pass protection is shaky, and quarterback Sam Leavitt can't stop giving away turnovers. The secondary was chasing all game, and the pass rush — which led the nation in sacks coming into the game — struggled to get Chambliss off his mark.

These things are all correctable, all part of a season-long journey that didn't end with a loss in the one moment LSU has built toward since Kiffin left Ole Miss holding a College Football Playoff bag last season. This was we LSU's we got him, and you don't moment.

It quickly evolved into the statement of statements for Ole Miss: We've got Chambliss, and you couldn't convince him to follow Kiffin — no matter how much money you threw at him.

Yeah, it's corny and contrived, but that's football in the south. That's how it works and how it bleeds and how it finally, fatefully, plays like you couldn't script it if you were Hemingway himself.

The good guys win, and the villain is vanquished.

And chokes on cold gumbo all the way home.

Matt Hayes is the senior national college football writer for USA TODAY Sports Network. Follow him on X at @MattHayesCFB . Listen to him daily, from 12-2 p.m., on 1010XL-Jacksonville .

articles.title: Florida Stuns Auburn in Wild SEC Showdown
articles.summary: The Florida Gators are officially 3-0. Florida traveled to Jordan-Hare Stadium on Saturday night and defeated Auburn 44-39 in a wild SEC opener, giving first...
articles.body:
Florida traveled to Jordan-Hare Stadium on Saturday night and defeated Auburn 44-39 in a wild SEC opener, giving first-year head coach Jon Sumrall his first conference victory with the Gators.

Florida wasted no time making its presence felt.

The Gators took a 7-3 lead in the first quarter after Jadan Baugh scored on a two-yard touchdown run. Duke Clark later added a 20-yard touchdown run, helping Florida build a 14-3 advantage.

Auburn fought back, but Florida carried a 20-17 lead into halftime.

The second half belonged to Jadan Baugh.

The Florida running back broke loose for a 33-yard touchdown early in the third quarter, pushing the Gators' lead to 27-17. After Auburn answered, Baugh struck again — this time on a 53-yard touchdown run that gave Florida a 41-24 advantage.

Baugh finished with 162 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 26 carries. It was his fourth consecutive 100-yard rushing game, dating back to last season.

Auburn scored 15 points in the fourth quarter and continued to pressure Florida until the final minutes. But the Gators' offense had built enough of a cushion to withstand the late push.

Quarterback Aaron Philo also delivered a strong performance, throwing for 204 yards and a touchdown while helping Florida finish with 495 total yards.

The victory is particularly significant because it came on the road against an SEC opponent. It was Florida's first win at Auburn since 1999 and ended a six-game road losing streak for the Gators.

Florida wasn't perfect — the Gators were penalized 16 times for 138 yards — but they consistently answered Auburn's biggest pushes.

Now, Florida returns home with a perfect record and plenty of momentum.

The Gators' next challenge will be another major one when Ole Miss visits Gainesville next Saturday.

Florida came into Jordan-Hare Stadium looking for a statement.

articles.title: Bristol Boils Over: Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar Trade Punches After Race!
articles.summary: The fireworks at Bristol Motor Speedway didn’t stop when the checkered flag flew. Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar got into a physical altercation on pit road...
articles.body:
The fireworks at Bristol Motor Speedway didn't stop when the checkered flag flew.

Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar got into a physical altercation on pit road Saturday night following the Bass Pro Shops Night Race, adding even more drama to an already chaotic night.

The tension started with 43 laps remaining.

Blaney had been one of the dominant drivers all night, leading a race-high 202 laps and winning Stage 2. He was battling near the front when Hocevar made contact with the rear of Blaney's No. 12 Ford. Blaney spun into the outside wall, ending his race and leaving him with a 33rd-place finish.

Hocevar continued on and eventually finished third.

After climbing from his damaged car, Blaney made it clear that he believed Hocevar was responsible for the wreck. Hocevar, however, defended his move and said he wasn't trying to wreck Blaney.

After the race, the disagreement turned physical.

Blaney approached Hocevar on pit road and shoved him. Hocevar immediately responded with punches, and Blaney fired back before members of both teams rushed in to separate the drivers.

Hocevar later explained that there wasn't much conversation before the fight broke out. He said Blaney approached him and that he wasn't going to simply stand there and take it.

Blaney, meanwhile, maintained that Hocevar hadn't lifted when the two made contact and that the crash cost him a chance to compete for the victory.

The fight overshadowed what had already been an incredible night of racing.

Joey Logano eventually won the race, with Kyle Larson finishing second and Hocevar recovering to finish third. Blaney's crash, however, completely changed the championship picture for the night.

Both Blaney and Hocevar are competing in the Chase, and the Bristol incident has added a new layer to their rivalry heading into the remaining playoff races.

Then Blaney and Hocevar made sure the drama continued after the checkered flag.

articles.title: 'War daddy' Jordan Hall sets gritty tone for MSU in return from injury
articles.summary: Jordan Hall made 13 tackles at Notre Dame to lead the MSU defense despite missing last week's game with a right arm injury.
articles.body:
SOUTH BEND, IND. — Jordan Hall walked to an open chunk of the field yelling, slamming his left arm down on his right like as if he were carrying a shield. The same right arm covered by a clunky, hinged brace. The one that nearly went limp on him when he hurt it two drives into the season opener. It suited him just fine.

Hall, a week after sitting out a game against Eastern Michigan with his right arm injury, came into Notre Dame Stadium and played his heart out for Michigan State (2-1). Thirteen times, Hall got in on tackles as Michigan State's defense hung tough with No. 3 Notre Dame (3-0). Ultimately, the Spartans lost, 27-10, but not without continued fight from their mike linebacker and his compatriots.

"He's going to be a pro. He's a captain. He's a war daddy," Michigan State coach Pat Fitzgerald said. "And I'm really, really, really proud of him. I mean, he is a hell of a player and a better person. So, we need him. He played great."

Hall knew by Wednesday, Sept. 16 there was a good chance he could get on the field Saturday, Sept. 19, and he didn't waste time making plays. After Notre Dame opened the game with a 61-yard bomb between quarterback CJ Carr and receiver Micah Gilbert, Hall rattled off three straight tackles to force a field goal.

If that play kept a few points off the board, it also put belief in his squad. The Spartans ' defense played with a swagger, keeping it a 17-10 game at halftime even after one of Alessio Milivojevic 's two interceptions threatened to spark a blowout.

"Everybody, from the beginning of the week, everybody had belief," Hall said. "I was just trying to play my part in getting the win today. Came up short."

Hall recorded nine solo tackles, and his 13 tackles more than doubled his next closest teammate. And as the Spartans weathered another injury to fellow linebacker Brady Pretzlaff before halftime, even Hall played through some discomfort as he tweaked his injury.

"It pops up here and there in some awkward positions that I'm in," Hall said, "but the braces helped me a lot. And yeah, it'll just be a progressive thing as we keep moving forward throughout the year."

Michigan State's defense had a tough night against a Notre Dame offense that jumped out to a 10-0 lead in the first 10 minutes. Carr threw for 234 yards and scampered in for a touchdown run. Gilbert had 170 of those yards on eight catches, and running back Nolan James Jr. ran for 121 yards on 26 carries.

But, Notre Dame had to wrestle — probably more than it expected as a nearly 30-point favorite — for the better part of four quarters. It wasn't a blowout, and in large part the reason was Hall and the Michigan State defense. He fit gaps hard against the run. He got into space for open-field tackles. And though his Spartans' pass rush generated one sack and one hurry, he and his fellow linebackers gave up just four catches for 18 yards to running backs and tight ends.

It took Notre Dame 17 plays to go 77 yards down the field for a field goal in the third quarter, a nearly 10-minute gauntlet that Hall played every snap. Even in the fourth, when Michigan State's own offense put up negative yardage, Hall and the defense allowed just a touchdown on three drives. He even took the time to hype up fellow captain Milivojevic, frustrated after a fourth-quarter interception on the first play of a drive.

"We just reminded him, you're a captain, you're a leader on this team," Hall said. "We're gonna get the ball back for you, so just calm down, be ready to go in a couple of minutes."

Hall may be hampered this season, but Michigan State's defense still looks better with him wearing pads and an arm brace than with him inactive on the sideline. After playing through last season injured and ailing, Hall has always shown a toughness to his game. But as a senior, he knows how important he is to this defense — and to Michigan State's larger aspirations.

"Everybody on the team believes in the guys that we have in the room," Hall said. "All the goals that we had on the table before the year are still on the table, and we're going to continue to try to achieve those goals."

Hall is going to try and make them happen, even if it hurts.

articles.title: 'For the Haters, Baby’: Joey Logano Wins at Bristol and Silences the Noise
articles.summary: Capitalizing on a late-race collision between frontrunners, the three-time champion snatched victory at the grueling Bass Pro Shops Night Race to cement his...
articles.body:
BRISTOL, Tenn. — Joey Logano just keeps finding ways to win.

On a wild and chaotic Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway , Logano took the Bass Pro Shops Night Race for his 40th career Cup Series victory and his third win of the 2026 season.

He led 93 of the 500 laps, including the first 81, and dominated Stage 1. The final lead only came with seven laps to go after frontrunners Ty Gibbs and Carson Hocevar made contact on a late restart. From there, Logano checked out and beat Kyle Larson to the line by 1.248 seconds.

The race itself was a grind — 3 hours, 2 minutes, and 18 seconds, with 13 lead changes and 10 cautions for 78 laps. In the middle of all that chaos, Logano did what he's always done: stay in position and capitalize when the opportunity showed up.

The win moved him up to third in The Chase standings, just 16 points behind new leader Kyle Larson. Three races into the postseason, Logano is right back in the middle of the championship fight.

As soon as he climbed out of the No. 22 Ford, he made sure everyone heard him.

"For the haters, baby," Logano said on the live broadcast. A few minutes later on USA Network he added, "Merry Christmas to me. I got a gift there."

That edge has always been part of his game.

Logano has three championships, all in even years — 2018, 2022, and 2024. This is another even year. He started 2026 quietly and still found himself in the thick of it by the time the lights came on at Bristol. Sixteen points out of the lead is nothing for a driver who knows how to peak at the right time.

For years people have dismissed those titles as products of the old playoff system . The narrative was that Logano benefited from the format more than he earned the trophies. Nights like this make that argument harder to keep making. He's winning when it counts, in the current system, against the best the series has to offer.

A lot of the post-race talk will center on the late contact between Hocevar and Ryan Blaney and the chaos that opened the door. That's fair — it was a messy ending. But you can't ignore what Logano did with the opportunity.

Champions don't always have the best car on the biggest nights. They put themselves in position to take advantage when the race breaks their way. That's exactly what happened Saturday.

This wasn't supposed to be his win when the final restart lined up. He made it his anyway.

Logano may not end up with a fourth title when the season is over. The field is deep and the next few weeks will be brutal. But he's not going quietly.

Three wins, 40 for his career, and a playoff picture that suddenly has the No. 22 right in the mix again.

The haters got their answer under the lights at Bristol.

Joey Logano is still here, still winning, and still dangerous.

The Tennessee Volunteers continued their strong start to the 2026 season Saturday night, cruising past Kennesaw State 42-9 at Neyland Stadium.

The Vols entered halftime leading 21-3, but the offense really began to pull away after the break.

With DeSean Bishop slowed by an injury during the game, Daune Morris stepped up in a major way.

Morris rushed for 116 yards on 14 carries and scored a touchdown, including a 42-yard touchdown run that helped Tennessee put the game out of reach.

Bishop still managed to find the end zone before leaving the game and later returned in the second half.

The Volunteers' defense also played a major role in the victory.

Kennesaw State struggled to consistently move the football, particularly during the first half. The Owls managed only 126 yards of offense through the opening 30 minutes, allowing Tennessee to build its lead without needing a perfect offensive performance.

Tennessee ultimately finished the night with another convincing victory and enters SEC play with a perfect 3-0 record.

Now the Vols get the game everyone has been waiting for.

Top-ranked Texas comes to Neyland Stadium next Saturday in Tennessee's first SEC game of the season. The matchup will provide Tennessee with its biggest test yet and give Brandon and the Volunteers an opportunity to make an early statement against one of the nation's top teams.

articles.title: ‘Beat by the team he built’ – Fans have no mercy for Lane Kiffin after LSU’s clutch loss to Ole Miss
articles.summary: The No. 8-ranked Ole Miss Rebels picked up a 32-24 win over the LSU Tigers in LSU head coach Lane Kiffin’s first game back in Oxford since leaving the progra...
articles.body:
The No. 8-ranked Ole Miss Rebels picked up a 32-24 win over the LSU Tigers in LSU head coach Lane Kiffin's first game back in Oxford since leaving the program.

Kiffin led the Rebels from 2020 to 2025, becoming a fan-favorite coach for consistently leading the program to success despite never being a premier recruiting destination.

Kiffin left the Rebels mid-season for the Tigers in November 2025 after a messy split. His first visit back to Oxford, ending in a loss, has allowed the Rebels' fanbase to demolish their former beloved coach.

Fans are going off on Lane Kiffin after LSU loses to Ole Miss

The Rebels picking up this win was a cathartic moment for their fans and neutral CFB fans who didn't appreciate how Kiffin abandoned the program for a flashier job at LSU.

"Lane Kiffin got beat by the team that he built and by the QB he recruited, and that wouldn't go to LSU with him," is what former NFL player Robert Griffin III had to say.

"Lane Kiffin needed Ole Miss. Ole Miss didn't need Lane Kiffin," said one fan .

"The fact Ole Miss isn't storming the field is soft. I want to see Lane Kiffin get tackled by a Sophomore," said another fan .

"Imagine what a good coach like Lane Kiffin could do at a school with resources like Ole Miss," said a fan joking about Kiffin leaving Ole Miss for those exact reasons and still losing to them.

"Lane Kiffin lost to the program he said couldn't get good players, to the quarterback that refused to follow him, in the stadium he said wasn't big enough. Tough," said another fan .

"All I have to say. Lane Kiffin left a great program, roster, and fan base to go chase NFL players in Louisiana. —– clown. Couldn't be happier for Golding and Ole Miss," said one fan .

Ole Miss jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the game, but Kiffin's Tigers fought back to tie the game at 24-24 in the second half, although the Rebels would retake a 32-24 lead.

Unfortunately, the Tigers threw an INT in the end zone with less than a minute to go to seal their loss.

Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers bet yet to pay off

Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU to chase championships in a college where the barometer for success is a title and not how many 10-win seasons one can earn over their career.

After leaving Ole Miss midseason, the team promoted DC Pete Golding to HC, who then led them on a deep postseason run. Now, he has beaten his former HC, Kiffin, in their first major clash.

The Rebels looked like the better team in the win as a more organised unit, whereas the Tigers are clearly hoping that their top-recruited talent can shine through in close games.

Unfortunately, structure won over flash, and Kiffin will have to wait for a while before getting the chance for a win as LSU coach in the 'Magnolia Bowl.'

articles.title: Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney brawl at Bristol after Bass Pro Shops Night Race
articles.summary: Bristol Motor Speedway earned its nickname after Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney fought following the Bass Pro Shops Night Race.
articles.body:
Bristol Motor Speedway earned "The Last Great Colosseum" moniker on Sept. 19 when Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar decided to throw punches following the Bass Pro Shops Night Race.

The fireworks began on Lap 457, when Hocevar wrecked Blaney out of the race in a battle for second place. Hocevar was looking to pass Blaney on the inside and Blaney tried to block. Hocevar didn't lift, and Blaney was sent spinning after making contact with the front of Hocevar's No. 77 car.

"I mean, I wasn't trying to wreck him," Hocevar said in a USA Sports post-race interview. "It just looked like to me, I had a run, he kind of went left and I spun him."

"We got clear off of (Turn) 4 and I tried to protect the bottom, and he crossed and never lifted, and I got crashed," Blaney said in a television broadcast interview after the initial wreck. "That's what I thought happened, and that's what it looked like happened."

Blaney led a race-high 202 laps and won Stage 2, but the crash resulted in a 33rd-place finish. Hocevar finished third behind winner Joey Logano and runner-up Kyle Larson.

But the battle between the two wasn't done.

Blaney approached Hocevar after the race and grabbed his fire suit, and Hocevar didn't wait to see what was coming. Hocevar's first right hand knocked Blaney's hat off; he connected a second one, and Blaney was dragged to the ground as people tried to separate the two drivers.

After a shouting match, Blaney lunged from a team member holding him back and tried to tackle him. He landed a left hand in the process.

"There wasn't a whole lot of talking. He just kind of said one thing and then went after me, and I wasn't going to take it," Hocevar said. "That was fun with the 54 (Ty Gibbs). I got ran into a lot for the win, and that was for second and he wants to come fight. I don't think anybody's left behind me, so they got an old-school Bristol show here."

articles.body:
South Carolina State continues its early-season hot streak, beating fellow FCS Top 25 team Furman 20-17 on the road. The Bulldogs controlled the game throughout. Furman withstood an early scoring blitz ( South Carolina State went up 14-0 early in the first quarter) to score a touchdown with two minutes and 27 seconds left in the fourth. But they ultimately weren't able to get the upper hand over a dominant and disciplined South Carolina State team and ultimately left with a loss.

Once again, South Carolina State's defense showed considerable dominance. Furman had only 53 rushing yards, which is uncharacteristic for a team that employs a stable of talented running backs and came into this game averaging 198.3 rushing yards per game. As they did against other opponents, South Carolina State's front four affected both the run game and Furman's quarterbacks: Connor Ackerley and Jake Garcia. Garcia was QB1 to start the season and got his fair share of action, throwing for 164 yards and Furman's only touchdown of the game to Luke Shields on 10 of 18 attempts.

Ben Croasdale, who emerged as one of Furman's best players heading into the game, had a very quiet night, with only 24 yards on eight carries. Furman had to rely on the passing game to get back in the game, but South Carolina State ultimately controlled the flow throughout.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

South Carolina State still has questions at quarterback, as Chennis Berry once again deployed a two-quarterback system at points in the game. Keely Watson was primarily QB1 throughout the night and finished with 186 yards, one touchdown, and one interception, on 12 of 25 passing.

Ronnie Robinson threw for 22 yards and had three carries for 15 yards. Still, the two-quarterback system is a bit confounding, particularly in a game as close as this one. Mason Pickett-Hicks was featured heavily in the run game, with 15 carries for 52 yards. But Josh Shaw ultimately punched in the touchdown for South Carolina State, once again solidifying himself as a home-run threat in the running back room alongside MPH.

This win solidifies South Carolina State's dominance and their seriousness as a top FCS program under Chennis Berry. While there's more work to be done for them to repeat as MEAC champions and ultimately Celebration Bowl champions, the 2026 South Carolina State team is arguably better than the past two years, and every week that goes by, it ultimately shows that statement is not blind conjecture.

The defense is stout in all phases. The special teams unit is deep, both in its punting placement and field-goal accuracy. And the running back room is as solid as any Chennis Berry-led team over the past five seasons, from his time at Benedict College to now his third year at South Carolina State. The only consistent question mark has been the quarterback room, and even then, Keely Watson has had phenomenal moments, including his lone touchdown throw for 65 yards to DJ Maltsby for the opening touchdown, just nine seconds into the game.

It's hard to see which team can stop South Carolina State's run . I'm not saying it's impossible, but the way South Carolina State is playing, being the latest HBCU team to finish the season undefeated is certainly on the board.

articles.title: Virginia Tech Takes Down Maryland in Statement Road Win
articles.summary: Virginia Tech made a statement in its first road test of the 2026 season. The Hokies defeated Maryland 35-26 on Saturday night in College Park, improving to...
articles.body:
Virginia Tech made a statement in its first road test of the 2026 season.

The Hokies defeated Maryland 35-26 on Saturday night in College Park, improving to 3-0 and giving new head coach James Franklin his first Power Four victory at Virginia Tech. The win also snapped Maryland's 20-game nonconference winning streak.

Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer delivered one of his best performances of the season.

Grunkemeyer threw for 314 yards and three touchdowns while also adding a rushing touchdown. He immediately gave the Hokies control, connecting with Luke Reynolds for a 14-yard touchdown on Virginia Tech's opening possession.

He later escaped the pocket on third-and-goal and ran for another score, giving the Hokies a 13-0 lead.

Virginia Tech's offense was extremely efficient early, scoring touchdowns on five of its first six possessions.

Hokies Pull Away Before Maryland's Rally

Virginia Tech took a 27-14 lead into halftime after Grunkemeyer found Ja'Ricous Hairston for a two-yard touchdown.

Jeffrey Overton Jr. also delivered a huge play, breaking free for a 49-yard touchdown reception that extended the Hokies' advantage.

Overton added another touchdown in the third quarter, this time on a two-yard rushing score, pushing Virginia Tech's lead to 35-14 heading into the fourth.

Maryland quarterback Malik Washington threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter touchdown passes to Dorian Fleming and Chris Durr Jr.

However, Maryland failed on both of its fourth-quarter two-point attempts. Those misses kept the Terrapins from getting within one possession and allowed Virginia Tech to hold on for the victory.

This was Virginia Tech's first Power Four matchup under Franklin, and the Hokies came through on the road.

After opening the season with wins over VMI and Old Dominion, Virginia Tech now sits at 3-0 heading into ACC play.

The Hokies will travel to Boston College next Saturday as they look to keep their perfect start alive.

Virginia Tech came into College Park looking for its first real test of the season.

articles.title: Ole Miss football news: Pete Golding gets last laugh vs. Lane Kiffin as Rebels takes down LSU
articles.summary: Emotions intensified before Ole Miss football faced LSU with Lane Kiffin making his return. Pete Golding earned a prime chance to take down his former Rebels...
articles.body:
Emotions intensified before Ole Miss football faced LSU with Lane Kiffin making his return. Pete Golding earned a prime chance to take down his former Rebels boss, yet had his composure tested amid a late Tigers rally. But Golding and Ole Miss earned the last laugh in escaping 32-24.

LSU erased a 24-7 deficit late with Kiffin leaning into new quarterback Sam Leavitt . Kiffin's QB even turned heads before the game with his name showing up on the pregame injury report as "doubtful." But Leavitt looked healthy in sparking 17 unanswered points, including tossing a 26-yard touchdown pass.

But LSU handed Ole Miss and quarterback Trinidad Chambliss too much time on the clock. Chambliss engineered a climactic final drive that included scaling a couple of third down scenarios. The dual-threat quarterback capped off the drive in scoring from 14 yards out with his legs.

Golding then rolled the dice and called for Ole Miss to go for two. JT Lindsey answered the call in taking the direct snap from center and punching it in, making it an eight-point game.

The defensive guru Golding, though, needed to get the Rebels to deliver one last stop. LSU faced a fourth down inside the Ole Miss red zone. But Ole Miss tipped the Leavitt pass into the air, falling into the hands of defensive back Jaylon Braxton to seal the win.

Ole Miss and Golding entered a more loud and hostile Vaught-Hemingway Stadium with Kiffin's return. Saturday marked his first appearance since the controversial exit from Oxford, leaving the Rebels before playing in the College Football Playoffs. Golding is proving he became the right guy to lead this team, as he's now 5-1 as a head coach.

articles.title: Colorado football served heaping helping of 'humble pie' in blowout loss at Northwestern
articles.summary: Northwestern earned a 41-7 blowout win over Deion Sanders' Colorado team on Saturday, Sept. 19.
articles.body:
EVANSTON, IL — Deion Sanders wanted to give his Colorado football team some humble pie, despite a 2-0 start to the season.

Northwestern did him one better, handing the Buffaloes an entire humble cake with a 41-7 beatdown on Saturday, Sept. 19, at Martin Stadium.

Colorado (2-1) opened the season with wins over Georgia Tech and Weber State. But Sanders reminded his team leading up to the game that it had not beaten anyone yet. The Wildcats (2-0) forced Colorado into four turnovers and scored 17 points off them. The Buffaloes also turned the ball over three times on downs, proving Sanders' point.

"Early in the week, I showed them the record of the two teams we had beaten and I told them we hadn't beaten anybody," Sanders said postgame. "Nothing against them, but you got to serve them humble pie when they're coming off a tremendous win."

That does not mean the Buffaloes came out flat or could not figure things out early. Colorado actually outgained Northwestern 199-188 in the first half, but three costly turnovers and two turnovers on downs led to it trailing 21-0 at halftime.

Penalties also undid the Buffaloes throughout the game. They had five called for 46 yards in the first half and then four more for 34 yards in the second half.

"We got to do better," Sanders said of the penalties. "Fifteen yards is 15 gasses. So they are going to be in shape and they are going to stop. Because it doesn't make sense, especially the self-inflicted (ones) that no one had nothing to do with you. Jumping offsides, like come on man, the play hasn't even started and that doesn't make sense. We'll get it right. I promise you, we'll get it right."

Even when the Buffaloes found an answer on JuJu Lewis' 50-yard touchdown pass to Joseph Williams early in the third quarter to cut the lead to 14 points, Northwestern had an answer, scoring the final 20 points of the game.

Northwestern finished with 423 yards of total offense, with 241 coming through the air and 182 rushing.

"Great game by Northwestern," Sanders said. "... (Chip Kelly) called a hell of a game. Flat-out butt kicking."

Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles — a Michigan State transfer — finished 17-of-22 passing for 241 yards and three touchdowns, while also adding two rushing scores.

"I'll tell you what, that kid played his butt off today," Sanders said of Chiles. "That's the best football game I've ever seen him play. That's not an insult, a shot at him, but he was effective. ... I'm happy for him and proud of him."

Lewis, Colorado's starter, finished the game 19-of-29 passing for 168 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Those were the first two interceptions of the 18-year-old's college career.

"It all starts with me. I am the quarterback," Lewis said. "It's my job to move the ball and score. ... We can obviously move the ball. I think we've seen that, but it's all about finishing. We can't score points, it doesn't matter. So just a lot to work on."

Deion Sanders frustrated with players on sideline

With his team being blown out of the stadium on Saturday, Sanders said postgame that he lit into some of his players on the sideline as the game started getting out of hand.

"I saw some guys fight, playing through it offensively and defensively," Sanders said. "Now you did see a couple of guys I got on because I don't understand how you can have joy in a loss. Especially when I'm upset. I'm walking right behind you. I don't understand. I can't ever understand that because I want to win every darn thing.

"I can't understand how in the world you can find joy or can find a laughing matter when I'm right behind you. I'm going to put my foot in it."
